controlPoints.lead: Answer 4 questions for each significant hazard — the system will suggest whether a critical control point is needed. For a CCP, set limits, monitoring and a responsible person.

controlPoints.q1: Are there measures that prevent this hazard?
controlPoints.q1hint: For example: temperature control, incoming inspection, separate equipment.
controlPoints.q2: Is this step specifically designed to eliminate the hazard or reduce it to an acceptable level?
controlPoints.q2hint: For example, heat treatment destroys microorganisms.
controlPoints.q3: Could the hazard at this step exceed an acceptable level?
controlPoints.q3hint: Think about what happens if the step goes wrong.
controlPoints.q4: Will a later step eliminate the hazard or reduce it to an acceptable level?
controlPoints.q4hint: If yes, control moves to that later step.

explain.ccp: Critical control point: the hazard is eliminated here, so it needs constant monitoring and limits.
explain.oprp: Operational prerequisite program: the hazard is controlled here but eliminated at another step.
explain.prp: General sanitation measures are enough — no separate point is needed.
explain.none: There are no preventive measures — review the step or the technology.

periodicity.hygiene: Before every shift — production staff; other staff — before entering the production area
periodicity.health_check: Before every shift — production staff; after illness — an additional check.
periodicity.climate_control: Daily, at the start and end of the shift — for each room.
periodicity.cold_equipment_control: Daily, at least twice per shift — for each piece of equipment.
periodicity.cleaning: Routine cleaning — every shift; deep cleaning — at least monthly, according to schedule.
periodicity.general_cleaning: Deep cleaning — at least once a month, according to the approved schedule.
periodicity.cleaning_ventilation_checklist: Ventilation cleaning — according to schedule, at least annually; condition checks — monthly.
periodicity.uv_lamp_runtime: Each time the unit is switched on — recording lamp operating hours.
periodicity.finished_product: Before serving each batch of finished products — by the food quality inspection committee.
periodicity.perishable_rejection: On receipt and before sale of each batch of perishable products.
periodicity.incoming_control: On receipt of every batch of food raw materials and food products.
periodicity.fryer_oil: Daily — before and after using frying fat.
periodicity.med_books: On hiring, then according to medical examination deadlines (Ministry of Health Order No. 29н).
periodicity.training_plan: Plan — for the calendar year; training — according to schedule, at least annually.
periodicity.staff_training: On hiring (induction briefing), then according to schedule, at least annually.
periodicity.ppe_issuance: Each time PPE is issued and when replaced at the end of its service life.
periodicity.sanitary_day_control: Sanitation day — at least once a month, according to the approved schedule.
periodicity.disinfectant_usage: Each time a disinfectant working solution is prepared or used.
periodicity.pest_control: Treatment — according to schedule, at least monthly; monitoring point checks — at every specialist visit.
periodicity.glass_items_list: Whenever the inventory of glass and brittle items changes, but at least annually.
periodicity.glass_control: Every shift — inspect glass and brittle items; unscheduled checks — after every breakage.
periodicity.equipment_maintenance: According to the maintenance schedule — at least annually for each piece of equipment.
periodicity.equipment_calibration: According to the verification schedule — by the deadline for each instrument, at least annually.
periodicity.equipment_cleaning: After every shift; cleaning with disassembly — according to the sanitation schedule.
periodicity.breakdown_history: When an event occurs — for every equipment fault and repair.
periodicity.metal_impurity: Every raw material batch undergoing magnetic inspection; magnet checks — every shift.
periodicity.incoming_raw_materials_control: On receipt of every batch of food raw materials.
periodicity.intensive_cooling: During every rapid cooling cycle for a prepared dish.
periodicity.product_writeoff: When an event occurs — for every product rejection and write-off.
periodicity.traceability_test: At least annually and after every change to the production process.
periodicity.accident_journal: When an event occurs — for every emergency (outage, leak, breakdown or other incident).
periodicity.complaint_register: As consumer complaints and claims are received.
periodicity.tableware_breakage: After every breakage of tableware or utensils — immediately after collecting the fragments.
periodicity.daily_samples: Daily — from each meal; refrigerate for at least 48 hours.
periodicity.vitaminization: On vitamin enrichment days — before serving the third (sweet) course.
periodicity.ration_control: Every 10 days or monthly — compare the actual food assortment with the prescribed standard.
periodicity.transport_temperature: Every trip — product temperature at loading and unloading.
periodicity.pool_water_control: Daily — before the pool opens, then according to the production control schedule.
periodicity.inventory_condition: According to the HACCP schedule (every shift or weekly) and whenever damage is found.
periodicity.instrument_sterilization: Every sterilization cycle — one record for each instrument load.
periodicity.medical_waste_b: When an event occurs — each time waste is collected, disinfected or handed over for removal.
periodicity.batch_release: For every finished product batch — before shipment.
periodicity.audit_plan: Plan — for the calendar year; internal audits — according to schedule, at least annually.
periodicity.audit_report: After every internal audit; management review — at least annually.

create-document.title: Create a document
create-document.body: Click “Create document”: the 15-day period and name are filled in automatically. Select the person conducting the examination. If automatic creation is enabled, the document is already in the list.

open-document.title: Open the document
open-document.body: Click the card for the required period to open the employee-by-day table.

add-staff.title: Add employees
add-staff.body: Choose “Add” → “Fill from employee list”. Each employee has two rows: examination and temperature.

staff-card.title: Expand the employee card
staff-card.body: Click the name to open the list of days.

status-cell.title: Record today’s examination
status-cell.body: Click today’s cell. Each click cycles through Healthy → Day off → Sick leave → Suspended → Holiday. Right-click to choose directly.

temperature-cell.title: Temperature above 37°?
temperature-cell.body: In the employee’s second row, “no” means normal and “yes” means above 37°.

autofill.title: Enable autofill
autofill.body: Every day at 06:00, everyone is marked “Healthy” and “temperature below 37”; days off, holidays and sick leave are filled automatically. Correct fever or illness the same day: previous days are locked.

finish.title: No need to save
finish.body: Every mark is saved immediately. When the period ends, choose “⋯” → “Close journal”.

create-document.title: Create a document
create-document.body: Click “Create document” and select the start date and responsible person. The name is filled in automatically.

open-document.title: Open the document
open-document.body: Click the card to open the journal with rooms and readings.

add-room.title: Add rooms
add-room.body: Choose “+ Add room” and select a storeroom from the directory. Temperature and humidity limits come from the room card. Only food storerooms are used.

journal-settings.title: Set the check time
journal-settings.body: Open “Journal settings” to set the measurement time (10:00 by default) and “Do not fill on days off”.

autofill.title: Autofill
autofill.body: The “Fill journal automatically” switch creates a row for each day and fills readings within the normal range. Manually entered values remain unchanged.

view-toggle.title: Switch to “Table”
view-toggle.body: On a phone, cards are for viewing only. Enter values in the table.

add-row.title: Add today’s row
add-row.body: If autofill is off, choose “Add row” and enter the date and who took the readings.

measure-input.title: Enter the readings
measure-input.body: Enter temperature (°C) and humidity (%) for each room. Values save when you leave the cell. A red value is outside the limits: a “Corrective actions” field appears below; describe what you did.

finish.title: Close the journal
finish.body: At the end of the month, choose “⋯” → “Close journal”. No need to save: everything is recorded immediately.

create-document.title: Create a document
create-document.body: Click “Create document”. The name and period are filled in automatically; check the responsible person.

document-card.title: Open the document
document-card.body: Click the card for the required period to open the journal table.

view-toggle.title: Choose a view on your phone
view-toggle.body: Use “Cards” to read and fill one entry at a time, or “Table” to see the entire journal as on paper.

add-row.title: Add an entry
add-row.body: The “Add” button above the table creates a row for the date, person who performed the task and readings.

fill-cells.title: Fill entries on the same day
fill-cells.body: Every value saves immediately; there is no separate “Save” button.

autofill.title: You can enable autofill
autofill.body: The “Fill journal automatically” switch fills past days and then keeps the journal automatically. Turn it off and you will be offered the option to remove the filled entries.

more-actions.title: Close the period
more-actions.body: When the period is complete, choose “⋯” → “Close journal”. The document moves to the “Closed” tab.

askSymptoms.title: Ask about symptoms
askSymptoms.body: Ask each employee about nausea, diarrhoea, fever, respiratory symptoms and pustular skin lesions. Suspend them if any answer is yes.

recordDecision.title: Record the decision
recordDecision.body: For each employee, enter “Healthy — cleared” or “Not cleared — reason”. A reason is required.

signAndTime.title: Sign and record the time
signAndTime.body: Add the examiner’s signature and the time at the end of the entry.

placeThermometer.title: Place the thermometer
placeThermometer.body: Open the door for no more than 10 seconds. Place the thermometer in the middle of the chamber, in the air rather than on a food shelf.

waitForReading.title: Wait for a stable reading
waitForReading.body: Hold the thermometer for 30–60 seconds until the reading stabilises. Use the final reading.

recordTemperature.title: Record the temperature
recordTemperature.body: Enter the current temperature for each refrigerator. If it is outside the normal range (0…+6°C for most refrigerators), record the actions and circumstances (increased load, malfunction or an open door).

correctDeviation.title: Act on any deviation
correctDeviation.body: Call an engineer, move the food and notify the manager if needed. Every deviation entry must include the measures taken.

clearArea.title: Clear the area
clearArea.body: Remove food residue and wipe tables, the cooker and chopping boards. Use labelled cleaning equipment, with separate tools for floors and tables.

washSurfaces.title: Wash with detergent
washSurfaces.body: Dilute the detergent according to its instructions. Treat surfaces thoroughly and allow 5–10 minutes of contact time.

rinseSurfaces.title: Rinse under running water
rinseSurfaces.body: Rinse off the detergent, especially from food contact surfaces.

recordCleaning.title: Record the cleaning
recordCleaning.body: Record the area, start and end times, product name and concentration, who cleaned and who checked. Sign the entry.

checkAppearance.title: Check the appearance
checkAppearance.body: Check colour, broth clarity, consistency, shape (a patty should be even and free of cracks) and garnish.

measureServingTemperature.title: Measure the serving temperature
measureServingTemperature.body: Hot dishes: at least 65°C. Cold starters: no more than 14°C. Drinks: according to the production procedure.

checkSmell.title: Check the smell
checkSmell.body: There must be no sour, rotten or rancid smell, only the smell characteristic of the dish.

tasteDish.title: Taste the dish
tasteDish.body: Check saltiness, doneness and any unusual aftertaste. Use a clean spoon every time.

compareDeliveryNote.title: Compare with the delivery note
compareDeliveryNote.body: Do the supplier, product name, quantity, production date and expiry date match the documents?

checkLabels.title: Check the labels
checkLabels.body: The packaging must show the manufacturer, ingredients, production date, expiry date, storage conditions and batch number. Reject it if these are missing.

measureTemperature.title: Measure the temperature
measureTemperature.body: Transport temperatures for perishables: dairy ≤ +6°C, meat ≤ +4°C, fish ≤ +2°C and frozen food ≤ -18°C. Record the reading.

inspectPackaging.title: Inspect packaging and goods
inspectPackaging.body: Check packaging integrity, swelling, mould and damage. Check colour and smell on arrival: both must be appropriate for the product.

recordStart.title: Record the cooling start
recordStart.body: When the dish is removed from the cooker, measure its temperature (it should be +65°C or above) and record the time. This is t0.

placeInChiller.title: Place in the chiller
placeInChiller.body: Use a blast chiller or a shallow container in a refrigerator. Do not seal tightly: steam must escape.

checkEveryHalfHour.title: Check every 30 minutes
checkEveryHalfHour.body: Measure the temperature: it should fall steadily. The target is +5°C within a maximum of 2 hours.

recordFinish.title: Record the finish
recordFinish.body: When +5°C is reached, record the time (t1) and temperature. Duration = t1 - t0.

recordStart.title: Start the fryer and record the time
recordStart.body: Record the start of use and the heating temperature.

checkOil.title: Check the frying oil
checkOil.body: Colour: no darker than amber. Smell: not rancid. If using a polar compound tester: < 24% is normal, 24–27% is a warning and > 27% requires immediate replacement.

recordDecision.title: Record the decision
recordDecision.body: “Use”: continue. “Replace”: drain the oil, wash the fryer and add fresh oil. Record the reason for replacement.

prepareSolution.title: Prepare the solution
prepareSolution.body: Dilute according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Follow the concentration on the label exactly.

treatSurface.title: Treat the surface
treatSurface.body: Apply the solution. Allow the specified contact time, usually 5–15 minutes (see the instructions).

rinseSurface.title: Rinse under running water
rinseSurface.body: Pay particular attention to food contact surfaces. Otherwise, chemical residues may remain in food.

recordTreatment.title: Record the treatment
recordTreatment.body: Record the area or equipment treated, the product, concentration, contact time and person who performed the treatment.

identifyNeeds.title: Identify what is needed
identifyNeeds.body: Issue according to employee requirements: gloves (1 pair/day), aprons (2–3/month) and a mask if handling ready-to-eat food.

issueForSignature.title: Issue against a signature
issueForSignature.body: Record the recipient’s full name, items issued, quantity, date and signature.

recordReplacement.title: Record replacements
recordReplacement.body: If PPE is worn out, record “Disposed of” and issue a replacement.

giveBriefing.title: Give the briefing
giveBriefing.body: Follow the programme. Induction at hiring covers hygiene and SanPiN requirements. Refresher training is every six months. Unscheduled training follows an incident or process change.

checkUnderstanding.title: Check understanding
checkUnderstanding.body: Ask 3–5 review questions. Retrain anyone who cannot answer.

recordTraining.title: Record the training
recordTraining.body: Record date, briefing type, topic, instructor’s full name, participants’ full names and everyone’s signatures. Without signatures the record is invalid.

registerBook.title: Register a new employee’s health book
registerBook.body: At hiring, record the book number, issue date, next examination date and hygiene certification date.

trackValidity.title: Track validity
trackValidity.body: Review the register weekly. If validity expires within 30 days, send the employee for a medical examination.

updateAfterExamination.title: Update after the examination
updateAfterExamination.body: Update the dates when the employee returns. If they did not pass, suspend them pending results.

disassembleEquipment.title: Disassemble the equipment
disassembleEquipment.body: Disconnect the power and dismantle parts (mincer blades, discs and attachments). Scrape food residue into a waste bin using a spatula or scraper.

washParts.title: Wash with detergent solution
washParts.body: Soak parts in hot detergent solution (40–45°C) for 10–15 minutes. Scrub thoroughly with a brush. Wipe the equipment housing with a cloth and solution.

rinseParts.title: Rinse with clean water
rinseParts.body: Running water must be ≥ 65°C: this is critical, so record the temperature in the journal. Remove all detergent residue.

disinfectParts.title: Disinfect
disinfectParts.body: Treat surfaces with disinfectant. Use the contact time in its instructions, usually 15–30 minutes. Do NOT rinse afterwards unless the product requires it.

checkDocuments.title: Check the documents
checkDocuments.body: The delivery note and consignment note must match on supplier, product name, quantity and production date. A quality certificate is required for every batch.

checkExpiry.title: Check expiry dates
checkExpiry.body: Check the production date and remaining shelf life at receipt. If less than 1/3 of the total shelf life remains, it is better to return the goods: there is little time to use them.

measureTemperature.title: Measure the temperature
measureTemperature.body: Dairy ≤ +6°C, chilled meat ≤ +4°C, chilled fish ≤ +2°C, frozen food ≤ -18°C. Use a contact thermometer at several points. Enter any deviation as a number in “Notes”.

inspectQuality.title: Check sensory quality
inspectQuality.body: Check appearance, colour, smell and packaging integrity. Signs of spoilage include mould, swollen packaging, darkening, unusual smell and damaged packaging.

receiveComplaint.title: Receive the complaint
receiveComplaint.body: Listen calmly without interrupting and thank the person for their feedback. Do not make excuses or deny anything: your task is to record it.

recordDetails.title: Record the details
recordDetails.body: Record the date, time, complainant’s full name and contact details if they consent, the subject (food, service or sanitary conditions) and an accurate account in their words.

notifyManager.title: Notify the manager
notifyManager.body: Notify them the same day. Complaints about sanitary conditions or food poisoning require IMMEDIATE reporting; the manager must be informed by the end of the working day.

recordActions.title: Record the measures taken
recordActions.body: Record what was done: refund, replacement dish, meeting with the manager, investigation or employee suspension. Include the deadline and responsible person.

prepareContainers.title: Take a clean jar for each dish
prepareContainers.body: Use a separate jar and spoon for every dish; never mix samples. Soup, main course, side dish, salad and drink each need their own container.

labelSample.title: Add and label the sample
labelSample.body: Keep a portioned dish whole; take at least 100 g of other dishes. Label with the dish, meal, sampling date and time.

refrigerateSample.title: Place in the sample refrigerator
refrigerateSample.body: Use a dedicated refrigerator or a separate labelled shelf, at +2…+6°C.

recordSample.title: Record the sample
recordSample.body: Click “Add”: enter the meal, dish, weight, sampling time and temperature. You can enter the disposal date immediately: 48 hours later.

coolDish.title: Cool the dish
coolDish.body: Add the vitamin to a cooled dish: boiling destroys it. Do not reheat the dish after adding it.

measureDose.title: Measure the dose for all portions
measureDose.body: Count portions using the menu plan and measure the preparation according to the dose per portion.

mixAndServe.title: Mix and serve
mixAndServe.body: Dissolve the preparation in a small amount of the dish, pour it into the main container and mix. Serve soon afterwards.

recordAddition.title: Record the addition
recordAddition.body: Record the dish, preparation, number of portions, amount added, time added and serving time.

calculateActual.title: Calculate actual use by food group
calculateActual.body: Add the food group’s consumption over the period and divide by the number of people served and the number of days to get grams per person per day.

recordNormAndActual.title: Enter the norm and actual amount
recordNormAndActual.body: Use one row per food group: norm, actual amount and percentage deviation.

explainDeviation.title: Explain any deviation
explainDeviation.body: If actual use is noticeably above or below the norm, explain why in the notes and describe the menu changes you will make.

measureAtLoading.title: Measure at loading
measureAtLoading.body: Insert the probe into a product from the middle of the batch. Cold food must stay cold and hot food hot. Record the temperature and time.

measureAtUnloading.title: Measure at unloading
measureAtUnloading.body: At the destination, measure the same products again and record the result.

reportDeviation.title: Report deviations
reportDeviation.body: If a product has warmed or cooled beyond acceptable limits, do not hand it over without the manager’s decision. Record this in the row.

stopNearbyWork.title: Stop nearby work
stopNearbyWork.body: If breakage occurs near exposed food or dishes, stop serving them and notify the shift supervisor.

collectFragments.title: Collect the fragments
collectFragments.body: Wear gloves and use a dustpan; collect small fragments with a damp cloth. Put them in a strong bag, label it “Glass” and remove it.

recordBreakage.title: Record the breakage
recordBreakage.body: Record what broke, how many items, where (dining room, kitchen or bar), the cause and “Fragments collected — Yes”.

takeSample.title: Take a sample
takeSample.body: Fill a clean flask from below the water surface, not the surface itself, away from chemical dosing points.

measureIndicators.title: Measure the indicators
measureIndicators.body: Measure free chlorine, combined chlorine and pH with a tester according to its instructions; measure temperature with a thermometer.

checkClarity.title: Check clarity
checkClarity.body: From the poolside, the markings and bottom in the deep area must be clearly visible.

recordAndCompare.title: Record and compare with limits
recordAndCompare.body: Enter readings in the journal. Use the limits in the pool’s production control programme. If a value is outside the limits, keep visitors out and notify the manager.

walkArea.title: Walk through the area
walkArea.body: Start with one work area: 1) boards and knives → 2) spatulas, whisks and ladles → 3) gastronorm trays and containers.

inspectEachItem.title: Inspect every item
inspectEachItem.body: Plastic: check for cracks, chips, deep cuts and peeling fragments. Metal: check for rust, burrs and broken parts.

removeDamagedItems.title: Remove damaged items
removeDamagedItems.body: Put damaged items straight into a box labelled “Withdrawn” and notify the shift supervisor. They must not be used.

recordInspection.title: Record the inspection
recordInspection.body: Use one row per inspected item or group: work area, item inspected, material, condition and action taken.

prepareInstruments.title: Prepare the instruments
prepareInstruments.body: 1) Soak instruments in disinfectant according to its instructions → 2) rinse under running water → 3) dry.

packWithIndicator.title: Pack and add an indicator
packWithIndicator.body: Place instruments in a kraft pouch with an indicator inside or alongside. Write the date on the pouch.

runCycle.title: Start the cycle
runCycle.body: Set the cycle according to the steriliser’s instructions (for example, dry heat at 180°C for 60 minutes). Wait until it finishes without opening the chamber.

checkIndicator.title: Check the indicator and record
checkIndicator.body: If the indicator changed colour, record instruments and quantity, method, cycle, “Indicator activated — Yes” and the steriliser. If not, repeat sterilisation and record that too.

collectSeparately.title: Collect separately
collectSeparately.body: Sharps (needles and blades) go only in a yellow puncture-resistant container; soft waste goes in a yellow bag. Do not mix with household waste.

disinfectWaste.title: Disinfect
disinfectWaste.body: Treat the waste according to the disinfectant instructions (solution and contact time), then close the packaging.

weighAndLabel.title: Weigh and label
weighAndLabel.body: Weigh the package and label it with the date and organisation name.

recordWaste.title: Record the waste
recordWaste.body: Enter waste type, weight in kg, disinfection method, packaging and recipient (organisation and handover document number).

takeSample.title: Take a sample
takeSample.body: Take several units from different parts of the batch.

checkProduct.title: Check the product
checkProduct.body: 1) Appearance, smell and taste → 2) label: name, date, expiry date and ingredients → 3) packaging integrity.

decideRelease.title: Make the decision
decideRelease.body: If everything is correct, select “Released”. If there is a nonconformity, select “Not released”, set the batch aside and notify the technologist.

recordRelease.title: Record the decision
recordRelease.body: Enter the product, batch number, quantity, checks performed and decision.

ensureSafety.title: Ensure safety
ensureSafety.body: Move the injured person to fresh air and call an ambulance if needed. Cordon off the danger area. For a chemical spill, evacuate first, then neutralise it.

assessFoodImpact.title: Assess whether food is affected
assessFoodImpact.body: If the incident affects food (glass in a dish, refrigerator outage > 3 hours or chemical contamination), ISOLATE it and DO NOT SERVE it. Write off all dishes from that batch.

notifyManager.title: Notify the manager
notifyManager.body: Immediately. Reporting any food incident or employee injury is required by the Labour Code and SanPiN. Serious cases (mass poisoning or death) require notifying Rospotrebnadzor within 12 hours (Article 50, Federal Law 52).

describeIncident.title: Describe it in the journal
describeIncident.body: Record the date and exact time, a factual account of what happened, equipment or food involved, injured people, immediate measures and the responsible person’s full name.

prepareArea.title: Prepare the area
prepareArea.body: Remove all staff from the room. UV-C is dangerous to eyes and skin: put up a warning sign and close the door.

switchOnLamp.title: Switch on the lamp
switchOnLamp.body: Record the switch-on time. The lamp’s service-life meter automatically records runtime if it has an electronic counter.

waitExposureTime.title: Allow the exposure time
waitExposureTime.body: Follow the device manual, usually 30–60 minutes for a 20 m² room. Use direct irradiation for air disinfection when no people are present.

switchOffAndVentilate.title: Switch off and ventilate
switchOffAndVentilate.body: Record the switch-off time. After UV treatment, air contains ozone: ventilate for 15–20 minutes before letting people in.

checkSchedule.title: Check the schedule
checkSchedule.body: Which area is scheduled today: kitchen, dining room, storeroom or toilet? Deep cleaning supplements daily cleaning; it does NOT replace it.

clearRoom.title: Clear the room
clearRoom.body: Remove everything movable, disconnect equipment and cover remaining items with film. Open windows for ventilation.

cleanTopToBottom.title: Clean from top to bottom
cleanTopToBottom.body: Ceiling → walls → lights → radiators → equipment → floor. For each surface: detergent solution → rinse → disinfect.

cleanRefrigerators.title: Clean the refrigerators
cleanRefrigerators.body: Fully defrost, wash with detergent, rinse, disinfect and dry. Check the door seals: clean separately if there is mould.

inspectHoodMonthly.title: Inspect the hood monthly
inspectHoodMonthly.body: Remove grease filters from the hood. Check grease buildup: if a filter barely passes air, soak it in hot detergent solution (60°C) for 2 hours, then rinse.

cleanHood.title: Clean the hood
cleanHood.body: Clean the inside and outside with degreaser and a cloth. Grease drips are a major cause of kitchen fires.

checkAirflow.title: Check the airflow
checkAirflow.body: Hold a tissue near the extraction grille: it should be drawn towards it. Weak airflow means blocked ducts; call a contractor urgently.

recordChecklist.title: Record in the checklist
recordChecklist.body: Enter date, filter condition (clean, moderate or greasy), airflow (normal or weak), work done and full name.

inspectInventory.title: Inspect against the inventory
inspectInventory.body: Walk through every item on the glass and brittle items list: dishes, measuring containers, lights in preparation areas, jars and bottles.

findDefects.title: Look for defects
findDefects.body: Look for chipped edges, cracks (especially hairline cracks), clouding and scratches with loose particles. Any such item must be written off in journal_writeoff.

checkLampCovers.title: Check lamp protection
checkLampCovers.body: All lights in food areas must have protective covers or shades. Replace any exposed bulb with a safe one immediately.

recordOutcome.title: Record the outcome
recordOutcome.body: If all is well, enter “Integrity intact” and sign. For a chip or crack, make a separate entry with the action taken (replaced, written off or isolated).

checkSchedule.title: Check the schedule
checkSchedule.body: Check the equipment manual for required maintenance and intervals. For example: refrigerator condenser cleaning and refrigerant checks every six months; fryer oil changes and heating element checks monthly.

performMaintenance.title: Perform the work
performMaintenance.body: In-house staff may perform routine cleaning and checks. Complex work (compressor or refrigerant replacement, electrical repairs) requires a licensed company.

recordMaintenance.title: Record in the journal
recordMaintenance.body: Enter date, equipment model and inventory number, work type, technician’s full name and any recommendations.

fileReport.title: File the service report
fileReport.body: For external maintenance, file the contractor’s original report and attach a copy to the journal.

registerInstruments.title: Keep an instrument register
registerInstruments.body: List all thermometers (contact, non-contact and refrigerator), scales, dishwasher pressure gauges and pH meters. Assign each an inventory number.

checkInterval.title: Know the verification interval
checkInterval.body: Check each instrument’s manual. A contact thermometer usually has a 1-year interval, scales 1 year and a non-contact thermometer 2 years.

sendForVerification.title: Send for verification
sendForVerification.body: 1 month before the certificate expires, send it to an accredited laboratory (Rostest, VNIIMS or a regional metrology centre). Obtain a verification certificate.

recordVerification.title: Record in the journal
recordVerification.body: Enter the verification date, certificate number, issuer, valid-until date, result (fit or unfit) and responsible person’s full name.

createEquipmentCard.title: Create a card for each unit
createEquipmentCard.body: Record model, serial number, inventory number, commissioning date, warranty period and service company.

recordBreakdown.title: Record every breakdown
recordBreakdown.body: Enter breakdown date, description of what failed, specialist call, repair date, parts replaced and cost.

analyseFrequency.title: Analyse the frequency
analyseFrequency.body: Repeated failures of the same kind indicate wear. Decide between an overhaul and replacement.

assessServiceLife.title: Assess service life
assessServiceLife.body: When total annual repair costs exceed 40% of a new unit’s price, replacement is economically justified.

cleanMagnet.title: Clean the magnet before the shift
cleanMagnet.body: Remove the magnetic separator, wipe it and reinstall it so the collected weight covers only this shift.

processBatch.title: Pass the batch through
processBatch.body: Pass raw materials through the magnet or detector. Afterwards, remove collected particles with tweezers into a clean container.

weighParticles.title: Weigh and record
weighParticles.body: Use analytical scales for the exact weight. Describe the particles: shavings, scale, nail or unknown material.

decideAction.title: Make the decision
decideAction.body: The Customs Union technical regulation limit is 3 mg of metal impurities per kg of raw material. Above this, batch quality is DOUBTFUL and laboratory testing is needed.

scheduleDrill.title: Run a drill every quarter
scheduleDrill.body: Choose a random sale from last week, for example “Chicken burger sold on 12 March at 14:30”.

traceToIngredients.title: Trace from dish to ingredients
traceToIngredients.body: Burger → patty → chicken → supplier delivery note No. 234 dated 5 March. Bread → bakery X batch. Sauce → batch Y. Identify the batch number for every ingredient.

traceToDishes.title: Trace from ingredients to dishes
traceToDishes.body: Chicken batch No. 234 (5 kg) → used for 50 patties → sold in 50 dishes during 5–7 March.

recordDuration.title: Record the time taken
recordDuration.body: Record how long it took to reconstruct the chain. The target is under 4 hours. Longer means the traceability system needs improvement.

recordReason.title: Record the reason
recordReason.body: Be specific: “expired on 23.03, batch 234”, “broken glass jar”, “storage temperature breach — meat turned bluish”, or “failed sensory check — sour smell”.

formCommission.title: Form a commission
formCommission.body: At least 3 people: production manager, storekeeper or commodity expert, and chef-technologist. They sign the report.

weighAndDescribe.title: Weigh and describe
weighAndDescribe.body: Record exact weight, product name, batch number, supplier and book value. The report is invalid without weight and value.

disposeProduct.title: Dispose of the product
disposeProduct.body: Perishables go to waste. Hazardous raw materials (suspected food poisoning) require separate contracted disposal. Never give them to staff to take home: this is a violation and risks poisoning outside work.

checkDocuments.title: Check the documents
checkDocuments.body: The delivery and consignment notes must match on amount, product name and date. Every item must have a declaration of conformity, mandatory for perishables.

measurePerishables.title: Measure perishable temperatures
measurePerishables.body: Dairy ≤ +6°C, meat ≤ +4°C, fish ≤ +2°C and frozen food ≤ -18°C. Measure at several points in the batch.

inspectQuality.title: Check sensory quality
inspectQuality.body: Check colour, smell and packaging integrity. Reject goods with signs of spoilage.

recordBatchAndExpiry.title: Record batch and shelf life
recordBatchAndExpiry.body: Record every batch separately for traceability. At receipt, at least 1/3 of the total shelf life must remain.

planDay.title: Plan the day
planDay.body: At least a week ahead, display a notice: “Closed for maintenance”. Publish the information on the website and social media.

emptyAndDefrost.title: Empty and defrost
emptyAndDefrost.body: Empty and defrost all refrigerators. Clear shelves and racks. Disconnect equipment and let it cool.

deepClean.title: Deep clean
deepClean.body: Clean walls and ceilings from top to bottom; air ducts if scheduled. Dismantle, wash and disinfect all equipment. Treat floors twice with disinfectant solution.

arrangePestControl.title: Arrange pest control
arrangePestControl.body: This is the best day for the pest control contractor: nobody is present, so treatment can proceed without risks to staff.

defineAuditAreas.title: Define audit areas
defineAuditAreas.body: CCP1 (incoming control), CCP2 (staff hygiene), CCP3 (sanitation), CCP4 (heat treatment), CCP5 (storage). Also check whether journals are maintained and documents are current.

appointAuditors.title: Appoint auditors
appointAuditors.body: Use internal staff trained in HACCP (GOST R ISO 19011 — audit fundamentals). Auditors must NOT inspect their own area.

setDates.title: Set the dates
setDates.body: Audit every area at least 1 time a year. Critical areas (heat treatment and personal hygiene) require audits every six months.

prepareChecklists.title: Prepare checklists
prepareChecklists.body: Prepare a list of questions for each area. Use GOST R 51705.1-2001 for the list of control points.

openMeeting.title: Hold the opening meeting
openMeeting.body: Inform the department that the audit is starting and present the objectives and plan. Record the start time in the minutes.

collectEvidence.title: Collect evidence
collectEvidence.body: Inspect areas using the checklist. Take photographs, interview staff and read journals. Record each observation as conforming, nonconforming or partially conforming, with justification.

recordNonconformities.title: Record nonconformities
recordNonconformities.body: Categories: critical (immediate correction; food safety threat), major (correct within 14 days) and minor (recommendation). Include evidence and a reference to the regulatory document for each.

closeMeeting.title: Hold the closing meeting
closeMeeting.body: Present all findings to the area manager and allow explanations. Include their explanations in the minutes.

writeSummary.title: Write a short summary
writeSummary.body: Use 1–2 paragraphs: what was audited, the overall conclusion (conforming, nonconforming or partial) and key risks.

listNonconformities.title: List nonconformities
listNonconformities.body: Create a table with number, category (critical, major or minor), description, evidence, regulatory reference, correction deadline and responsible person.

planCorrectiveActions.title: Plan corrective actions
planCorrectiveActions.body: For each nonconformity, state how to correct it and prevent recurrence. A report without the ROOT CAUSE is incomplete.

submitToManagement.title: Submit to management
submitToManagement.body: Give the original to the director, a copy to the audited area’s manager and another copy to the audit file.

defineTopics.title: Define the topics
defineTopics.body: Mandatory: personal hygiene and HACCP basics for everyone, fire safety and occupational safety. Specialist topics: particular equipment and new recipes.

groupStaff.title: Group the staff
groupStaff.body: Cooks, cleaners, storekeepers and the production manager each need their own topics and level of detail.

setFrequency.title: Set the frequency
setFrequency.body: Basic hygiene and HACCP training: at hiring and annually. Specialist topics: as planned. Unscheduled training: after an incident or a change in technology.

chooseFormat.title: Choose the format
chooseFormat.body: Internal training led by the production manager, external training at a specialist centre, or self-study with video and a test.

walkAllAreas.title: Walk through all areas
walkAllAreas.body: Kitchen (hot and cold sections), washing area, storeroom, bar and dining room. Account for glass items everywhere food is present.

listAllItems.title: List every item
listAllItems.body: Include glass dishes (carafes and jars too), measuring vessels (jugs and beakers), glass thermometers, bulbs and shades, bar bottles and spice jars.

assignNumbers.title: Assign numbers
assignNumbers.body: Give every item a number, with a sticker on the container or in its area. This makes missing items easy to find during the daily glass_control check.

recordLocation.title: Record the location
recordLocation.body: Enter the area and shelf or cabinet. “Refrigerator No. 2, top shelf” is a precise location.

inspectMonthly.title: Inspect internally every month
inspectMonthly.body: Check behind refrigerators, under cookers, storeroom corners, waste bins, ventilation and toilets. Look for rodent droppings, gnawed packaging and cockroach signs (live insects, shed skins or smell).

recordFindings.title: Record findings
recordFindings.body: If there are no signs, enter “Inspection completed, no signs of pests found” and sign. Otherwise, record the location and urgently call a specialist organisation.

scheduleTreatment.title: Schedule insect and rodent control
scheduleTreatment.body: Under the contract, at least 1 time a quarter. The contractor treats the premises and leaves a completion report and protocol listing products, concentrations and application sites.

fileReports.title: File the reports
fileReports.body: Put a dated copy of the contractor’s report in the pest control journal and the original in the “Contracts” folder. Rospotrebnadzor requests the original during inspections.

employeeAccess.answer: No. Scanning a QR sticker with a phone camera opens the relevant log. Employees select their name and confirm the entry with their personal 4–6 digit PIN. No app installation or workspace login is needed.

missedEntry.question: What happens if an employee misses a log entry?
missedEntry.answer: The entry stays empty and the service detects it. The manager receives a Telegram reminder at 12:00, another reminder and an email at 17:00, and an urgent alert at 21:00. At the end of the shift, those responsible for the hygiene log receive a list of employees who have not checked in.

qrSecurity.question: How are QR entries verified?
qrSecurity.answer: Entries are confirmed with the employee’s personal PIN. Five incorrect attempts lock entry for 15 minutes. The server records the time, and the audit log records who entered what and when. Each refrigerator has its own sticker; the equipment cannot be changed in the form.

electronicLogs.question: What is a digital food safety log?
electronicLogs.answer: A web service where employees enter the same records they used to keep in paper logs: hygiene, temperatures, product checks and more. Electronic records are expressly permitted by SanPiN 2.3/2.4.4282-26, “Sanitary and Epidemiological Requirements for Public Catering,” which took effect on 1 September 2026 and replaced the previous SanPiN 2.3/2.4.3590-20.

inspection.question: How does a Rospotrebnadzor inspection work?
inspection.answer: The inspector receives a PDF export with all records for the requested period. The print format includes the required details: full name, job title, electronic signature, date and key values.

integrations.question: Does it sync with iiko and 1C?
integrations.answer: Yes. Suppliers, products, deliveries and product checks sync automatically, so you do not have to enter them by hand. Setup takes about 30 minutes with our engineer.

offline.question: What happens if the internet goes down?
offline.answer: Nothing serious: the interface keeps working on the tablet, records are saved locally and sent to the server automatically when the connection returns. Wi-Fi problems will not cause you to miss a shift.

dataSecurity.question: Is my data secure?
dataSecurity.answer: All logs are stored in a protected PostgreSQL database on servers in Russia. Backups are made every 6 hours. Data is transmitted over HTTPS with TLS 1.3. Access requires a username and password and follows role-based permissions; PDF exports for inspections are available only to administrator accounts.

import.question: Can I import data from Excel or paper?
import.answer: Yes. Import employees, equipment and suppliers from an Excel spreadsheet. Keep your old paper records and create new ones in WeSetup; you can also choose paid digitization of your archive.

page.guideNewMonth: You do not need to create a new month. The schedule is built for any month from each employee’s weekly days off—the Mon–Sun chips in their row. Use the arrows to change the month; the schedule is filled in automatically. Cover shifts, days off, and extra shifts can be marked in a cell and override the weekly rule for that day only.
page.guideWorkOff: On a regular day off, the employee receives no daily tasks or reminders, and the Hygiene Log marks the day with “O”. Tasks remain available in the app if the employee covers a shift.
page.guideVacation: During vacation, the Hygiene Log marks the day with “Vac”. Telegram reminders are paused, and the employee is not counted as having missed tasks on the monitoring panel. Tasks remain available in the app in case they cover a shift.
page.guideSickLeave: During sick leave, the Hygiene Log marks the day with “S/L”. Telegram reminders are paused, and the employee is not counted as having missed tasks on the monitoring panel. Tasks remain available in the app if they return early.
page.guideDismissal: On the specified date, the employee moves to the “Archive”: they disappear from assignee lists and new journal rows and stop receiving tasks and reminders. Existing records remain available for inspection.

aiConnect.title: AI assistants & API
aiConnect.description: Connect ChatGPT, Claude or your developer — check journal status, fill cells and add employees right in the chat.

guide.title: How it works
guide.b1: Create a key — it acts with your permissions and only in this organization.
guide.b2: Paste the link or key into ChatGPT, Claude or Cursor — step-by-step guide below.
guide.b3: Talk to the assistant in plain language: it finds the right journal, document and employees itself.
guide.a1: We store only a fingerprint of the key, and you can revoke it in one click. Every entry made through AI appears in the activity log with the key name.
guide.a2: Marks in grid journals (employee × day) and new employees — by the same rules as the interface. It never changes closed days or documents and does not invent measurement values.
guide.q3: How is MCP different from the API?
guide.a3: MCP is the standard that lets AI assistants use the service on their own. The REST API is for your developer: the same operations as plain HTTP requests, described in OpenAPI.

balance.title: Balance and rewards
balance.inAppDescription: Your organization’s reward points and points history.
balance.description: Use points to pay for your subscription: 1 point = ₽1. Earn them by recommending the service to colleagues and leaving reviews, or add funds to your balance. Points are applied automatically when you pay.

guide.title: How points work
guide.onePointBody: Points stay in the organization balance and are spent when paying for a subscription. Equipment cannot be purchased with points.
guide.inviteBody: When a colleague subscribes, you receive {percent, number}% of its price in points. One reward is paid per invited business.
guide.reviewBody: Text review: ₽300; with a photo: ₽750; with a video: ₽1,990. Anonymous reviews without a name or business earn 20% less. Points are credited after moderation.
guide.topupBody: Pay by card or business invoice, from {min, number} to {max, number}. Funds are credited as points at 1:1 as soon as payment is confirmed. Promo codes and offers do not apply to top-ups.
guide.faqBurnAnswer: No. They remain in your balance until you spend them on a subscription.
guide.faqWithdrawQuestion: Can I withdraw points as money?
guide.faqWithdrawAnswer: No. Points cannot be withdrawn; they can be used to pay for a subscription. If you added funds by mistake, contact support@wesetup.ru.
guide.faqEquipmentQuestion: Can I pay for equipment with points?
guide.faqEquipmentAnswer: No. For an order with a subscription and equipment, points cover only the subscription; equipment is paid for with money.
guide.faqAutopayQuestion: Why can’t I use points for automatic renewal?
guide.faqAutopayAnswer: The payment service saves your card using the first payment amount. If points reduced that amount, later automatic charges would no longer match the plan price.

sanpinReference.title: SanPiN reference
sanpinReference.description: Key standards for food production (SanPiN 2.3/2.4.4282-26, GOST R 51705.1-2024, TR CU 021/2011)

temp_fridge.title: Cold room temperature
temp_fridge.description: Perishable foods must be stored at +2...+6°C

temp_freezer.title: Freezer temperature
temp_freezer.description: Frozen foods must be stored at a temperature no higher than -18°C

temp_hot_food.title: Hot food serving temperature
temp_hot_food.description: The temperature of hot dishes at serving must be at least +65°C

temp_cold_food.title: Cold food serving temperature
temp_cold_food.description: The temperature of cold dishes and starters at serving must not exceed +15°C

temp_cooking_meat.title: Meat product core temperature
temp_cooking_meat.description: The core temperature of meat and meat products during heat treatment must be at least +85°C

temp_cooking_poultry.title: Poultry core temperature
temp_cooking_poultry.description: The core temperature of a poultry carcass must be at least +85°C

temp_pasteurization.title: Milk pasteurization
temp_pasteurization.description: Pasteurize at +72...+76°C for 15-20 seconds, or at +63°C for 30 minutes

temp_transport.title: Temperature during transport
temp_transport.description: Perishable foods are transported in refrigerated vehicles at +2...+6°C

shelf_salads.title: Salad storage time
shelf_salads.description: Dressed salads — no more than 1 hour; undressed salads — no more than 6 hours at +2...+6°C

shelf_cooked_meat.title: Cooked meat storage time
shelf_cooked_meat.description: Boiled or fried meat — no more than 24 hours at +2...+6°C

shelf_dairy.title: Dairy product storage time
shelf_dairy.description: Pasteurized milk — up to 10 days; cottage cheese — up to 72 hours at +2...+6°C

incoming_docs.title: Documents required on receipt
incoming_docs.description: When receiving products, check the consignment note, declaration/certificate of conformity, and veterinary certificate (for animal-origin products in the Mercury federal information system)

incoming_packaging.title: Packaging inspection
incoming_packaging.description: Products must not be accepted if packaging is damaged, labelling is missing, the expiry date has passed or temperature requirements have not been met

incoming_temp_check.title: Temperature measurement on receipt
incoming_temp_check.description: Temperature measurement is mandatory when receiving perishable products: meat ≤ +4°C, fish ≤ -18°C, dairy products ≤ +6°C

hygiene_medbook.title: Personal medical record
hygiene_medbook.description: All food production employees must have a personal medical record containing confirmation of medical examinations and hygiene training
hygiene_medbook.document: Russian Ministry of Health Order No. 29н of 28.01.2021

hygiene_daily_check.title: Daily pre-shift health check
hygiene_daily_check.description: Before work starts, check for pustular skin diseases on the hands, acute respiratory illness and intestinal infections. People with signs of illness must not be allowed to work

hygiene_hands.title: Handwashing
hygiene_hands.description: Handwashing is mandatory when entering the production area, after using the toilet, after handling raw food and when moving from one operation to another

cleaning_routine.title: Routine cleaning
cleaning_routine.description: Routine wet cleaning of production areas — at least 2 times per shift. Floors — as they become dirty; walls and equipment — daily

cleaning_general.title: Deep cleaning
cleaning_general.description: Deep cleaning of all rooms — at least 1 time per month using detergents and disinfectants

cleaning_equipment.title: Equipment sanitation
cleaning_equipment.description: Production equipment, utensils and containers must be washed with detergents after every production operation

haccp_plan.title: Mandatory HACCP plan
haccp_plan.description: All businesses producing food must develop, implement and maintain procedures based on HACCP principles
haccp_plan.penalty: Fine of up to 300 000 RUB; suspension of operations for up to 90 days (Article 14.43 of the Russian Code of Administrative Offences)

haccp_ccp.title: Critical control points
haccp_ccp.description: A CCP is a step at which a control measure can be applied to prevent or eliminate a food safety hazard, or reduce it to an acceptable level

haccp_monitoring.title: CCP monitoring
haccp_monitoring.description: A monitoring system must be established for each CCP: what is monitored, how, by whom and how often

haccp_corrective.title: Corrective actions
haccp_corrective.description: If there is a deviation from critical limits, isolate the batch, decide its subsequent disposition, identify the cause and repeat monitoring

calibration_frequency.title: Thermometer verification frequency
calibration_frequency.description: Liquid thermometers — 1 time per year; electronic thermometers — 1 time every 2 years. Scales — 1 time per year
calibration_frequency.document: Ministry of Industry and Trade Order No. 2386

pest_frequency.title: Insect and rodent control frequency
pest_frequency.description: Preventive rodent control — at least 1 time per month; insect control — as needed, but at least 1 time per month during the warm season

writeoff_procedure.title: Write-off procedure
writeoff_procedure.description: Products past their expiry date or showing clear signs of spoilage must be immediately withdrawn from circulation and disposed of. A write-off record must state the reason and disposal method

electronic_journals.title: Use of electronic journals
electronic_journals.description: Electronic production control journals are permitted provided that the person making entries can be identified and unauthorized data changes are prevented

hygiene.intro: Daily staff checks before the shift. Confirm readiness to handle food: clean uniforms, no cuts and no respiratory infection symptoms. Mark each person as “Cleared” or “Not cleared”.
hygiene.whoFills: The head chef, production manager or shift supervisor conducts the examination and completes the journal. It usually takes 5–10 minutes in the morning.
hygiene.whenToFill: Every working day before the shift starts, preferably before 09:00 and before employees begin handling food.

prepare.staffList: Today’s staff list (loaded automatically from the system)
prepare.lighting: Good lighting in the changing room or examination room

gatherStaff.title: Gather all staff in the morning
gatherStaff.body: Front-line staff: cooks, kitchen workers, cleaners, sales assistants and waiters. Everyone who will handle food or dishes.

inspectHands.title: Inspect hands
inspectHands.body: Hands must be visibly clean, without fresh cuts, abrasions or pustules. Nails must be short, without polish or artificial nails. No jewellery (rings or bracelets).
inspectHands.tip: A fresh cut on a finger means NO work with exposed food. Assign work unrelated to cooking, such as washing dishes while wearing gloves.

checkUniform.title: Check uniforms and appearance
checkUniform.body: Clean, unstained uniforms, hair covered by headwear and no strong perfume. Women should have their hair tied back.

askSymptoms.title: Ask about symptoms
askSymptoms.body: Ask about respiratory infection symptoms (cough, runny nose, fever), intestinal infection (diarrhoea or vomiting in the last 48 hours) and skin rashes. Employees must report these themselves.
askSymptoms.tip: Under SanPiN 2.3/2.4.4282-26, staff with infection symptoms are suspended until they recover and provide a doctor’s certificate.

recordDecision.title: Mark “Cleared” or “Not cleared”
recordDecision.body: If there is a problem, clear the checkbox and describe it in the comment, for example “Ivanov I. — cough, temperature 37.5, suspended”.

saveResult.title: Save the result
saveResult.body: Click “Save” at the bottom. The journal moves automatically to “Closed for today” and TasksFlow stops sending reminders.

allCleared.label: Everyone cleared
allCleared.value: All ✓, comment: “Full shift team present, no concerns”

oneSuspended.label: One person suspended
oneSuspended.value: Ivanova E. — unchecked, comment: “t°=37.4, runny nose. Sent home; replacement: Petrova K.”

mistakes.recordingFromMemory: Completing it from memory in the evening: the journal must record the morning examination, not a later reconstruction
mistakes.clearingFingerCut: Clearing someone with a plaster on their finger is a violation: gloves are required and they must not handle exposed food
mistakes.markingAbsentStaff: Staff on days off or sick leave must not be included in the examination; leave their marks blank

hiddenSymptoms.trigger: An employee arrives with infection symptoms and denies them
hiddenSymptoms.action: Use a non-contact thermometer. If the temperature is >37.0, suspend the employee and require a doctor’s certificate before their return.

openWound.trigger: A cook has an open wound on their hand
openWound.action: Use a waterproof dressing and gloves until the end of the shift. If this recurs, assign light duties such as dishwashing.

hygiene.legalRef: SanPiN 2.3/2.4.4282-26, “Sanitary and epidemiological requirements for public catering”.

health_check.intro: The health journal records daily clearance to work with food. It confirms that before the shift the employee has no signs of infectious disease, pustular skin lesions or cuts on their hands. Complete it alongside the hygiene examination: one round, two records.
health_check.whoFills: The production manager, head chef or shift supervisor: the same person who conducts the hygiene examination.
health_check.whenToFill: Every working day before the shift and before the employee handles food. The system automatically creates a document for a 15-day period.

prepare.lighting: Good lighting in the examination area

gatherShift.title: Gather the shift before work starts
gatherShift.body: Examine everyone who handles food, dishes or utensils: cooks, kitchen workers, pastry chefs, cleaners, waiters and sales assistants. Do not mark absent staff (holiday, day off or sick leave); leave their row blank.

askSymptoms.title: Ask about health and symptoms
askSymptoms.body: Ask directly about fever, sore throat, cough, runny nose, nausea, vomiting or diarrhoea in the last 48 hours, and yellowing of the skin or eyes. Staff must also report intestinal infection in a family member.
askSymptoms.tip: “Fine” is not enough: ask every question on the list. This is how an inspector asks during a check.

measureTemperature.title: Measure temperature
measureTemperature.body: Use a non-contact thermometer on the forehead or wrist. At 37.0°C or above, the employee is not cleared until the cause is established.

inspectSkin.title: Inspect hands and exposed skin
inspectSkin.body: Check palms, fingers, between fingers and forearms for cuts, abrasions, burns, pustules, boils, peeling and rashes. Nails must be short, with no polish or extensions, and hands free of jewellery.
inspectSkin.tip: A cut does not automatically mean exclusion from the shift. Cover it with a waterproof plaster and a glove, but prohibit work with exposed food that day.

recordDecision.title: Decide and record in the journal
recordDecision.body: For each employee, enter “Healthy, cleared” or “Not cleared”. For anyone not cleared, specify symptoms, temperature, action taken (suspended, referred to a doctor or moved away from food handling) and their replacement.

saveAndDocument.title: Save and document any suspension
saveAndDocument.body: Click “Save” to record the date and author. For a suspension, update the replacement in the shift schedule. Before the employee returns, require a doctor’s certificate and attach its scan to the medical books journal.

healthyShift.label: Shift with no concerns
healthyShift.value: All employees: “Healthy, cleared”. Comment: “Shift of 6, no complaints, temperatures normal, skin clear”.

respiratorySuspension.label: Suspension for respiratory symptoms
respiratorySuspension.value: Sidorova A. — “Not cleared”. Comment: “t=37.6, sore throat, cough. Sent home at 08:15; doctor’s certificate required to return. Replacement: Ivanova M.”

fingerCut.label: Cut on a finger
fingerCut.value: Kuznetsov P. — “Cleared with restrictions”. Comment: “Cut on left index finger, covered with a waterproof plaster. Washing dishes in gloves; not cleared to handle exposed food”.

mistakes.weeklyRetrospective: Completing the entire week in the evening: records must be made each working morning
mistakes.bulkClearanceWithoutInspection: Marking everyone healthy in one click without examining them: the most common inspector complaint
mistakes.missingSuspensionReason: Omitting the reason for suspension: “Not cleared” without a comment does not prove that action was taken
mistakes.glovesOverPustule: Allowing someone with a pustule on their hand to work in gloves: pustular skin disease prohibits all food handling
mistakes.markingAbsentStaff: Marking employees who were not at work that day

vomitingDiarrhoea.trigger: An employee has vomiting or diarrhoea
vomitingDiarrhoea.action: Suspend immediately and exclude them from production areas. Return requires a doctor’s certificate. If two or more people develop symptoms during a shift, notify the manager: this may be an outbreak requiring notification to Rospotrebnadzor.

pustularLesion.trigger: Pustular skin lesion on the hands
pustularLesion.action: Exclude completely from handling food and dishes until healed. A glove does not solve the risk of staphylococcal contamination of food.

hiddenMidShift.action: Suspend the employee and withdraw products they touched with bare hands from sale. Record the discovery time and list of withdrawn items in the journal.

health_check.legalRef: SanPiN 2.3/2.4.4282-26, “Sanitary and epidemiological requirements for public catering”, clauses 2.21–2.22; Ministry of Health Order No. 29n of 28.01.2021.

med_books.intro: A register of all employees’ medical books, with issue dates and upcoming recertification dates. Its main purpose is to prevent an expired medical book from being overlooked.
med_books.whoFills: The manager or HR department maintains the register and monitors deadlines.
med_books.whenToFill: When each employee is hired, during the annual bulk update and on expiry (every 2 years for catering).

registerEmployee.title: Add the employee to the register
registerEmployee.body: Enter full name, job title, medical book number, issue date and next medical examination date.

uploadScan.title: Upload a scan of the medical book
uploadScan.body: Upload a PDF or JPG of the stamped spread. It is kept for the sanitary inspector.

setReminder.title: Set a reminder
setReminder.body: The system sends a Telegram push notification 30 days before expiry. Do not ignore it: staff cannot work a shift without a valid medical book.

validBook.label: Valid medical book
validBook.value: Ivanova M. S., cook. Medical book No. 77-123456, issued 14.03.2025, next examination 14.03.2026, hygiene certification 14.03.2026. Scan attached.

upcomingExpiry.label: Expiry approaching
upcomingExpiry.value: Petrov A. V., kitchen worker. Examination due by 02.05. Comment: “Booked for examination on 21.04; referral issued”.

newEmployeeWithoutBook.label: New employee without a medical book
newEmployeeWithoutBook.value: Sokolova E. — medical book being processed. Not cleared for food handling until the book with a clearance mark is received.

mistakes.onlyIssueDate: Tracking only the issue date and ignoring the next medical examination date
mistakes.combinedScan: Keeping one combined scan instead of attaching each scan to its employee
mistakes.missingHygieneCertification: Allowing a shift without a hygiene certification mark
mistakes.dismissedEmployees: Not removing dismissed staff: the actual headcount no longer matches the timesheet
mistakes.ignoredReminder: Ignoring the 30-day reminder: a medical examination cannot be completed in one day

expiredBook.trigger: Medical book expired more than 7 days ago
expiredBook.action: Suspend from food handling. Book the examination today: the medical assessment takes 1–3 days.

med_books.legalRef: Ministry of Health Order No. 29n of 28.01.2021, “Approval of the procedure for mandatory medical examinations”.

climate_control.intro: Monitor temperature and humidity in production and storage rooms to confirm that food storage and preparation conditions meet the required standards.
climate_control.whoFills: The duty cook, technologist or commodity expert, depending on the room. In the kitchen, the cook; in the storeroom, the storekeeper.
climate_control.whenToFill: 2–3 times per shift in production areas; once a day in storerooms.

prepare.thermometer: Verified thermometer with a verification mark no older than 1 year

prepareMeters.title: Take a thermometer and hygrometer
prepareMeters.body: Check that verification is current. The sanitary inspector will not accept data from an unverified instrument.

measureLocations.title: Measure at several points
measureLocations.body: Avoid doors, air-conditioner airflow and direct sunlight. Ideally, measure in the middle of the room at chest height.

recordReadings.title: Record readings
recordReadings.body: Record temperature and humidity at each point. Compare with the limits:
recordReadings.tip: Hot kitchen: 18–24°C, 40–60% RH. Cold kitchen: 12–18°C, 40–60% RH. Dry store: 10–18°C, up to 70% RH.

correctDeviation.title: If outside the limits
correctDeviation.body: In “Corrective action”, describe what you did: opened a window, turned on air conditioning or moved food to another room.

normal.label: Within limits
normal.value: Cold kitchen: t°=14.2°C, RH=52%. All OK.

exceeded.label: Limit exceeded
exceeded.value: Hot kitchen: t°=27°C (limit ≤24). Action: extra extraction switched on; cooker stopped for 20 min. After 30 min, t°=23°C, within limits.

mistakes.guessingReadings: Estimating without a thermometer: the inspector requires a verified instrument
mistakes.tooFewChecks: One reading a day in a hot kitchen is insufficient; at least 2 are needed
mistakes.missingCorrectiveAction: Failing to record corrective action when a limit is exceeded

climate_control.legalRef: SanPiN 2.3/2.4.4282-26; Customs Union Technical Regulation 021/2011, Article 10.

cold_equipment_control.intro: Temperature checks for refrigerators and freezers. This is a HACCP critical control point: temperature breaches risk the growth of salmonella, listeria and other pathogens.
cold_equipment_control.whoFills: The duty cook or kitchen worker, at opening in the morning and closing in the evening. Large kitchens assign a separate employee to each area.
cold_equipment_control.whenToFill: At least twice daily, morning and evening. Under SanPiN, every 4 hours during the production day.

prepare.equipmentList: List of refrigerators and their limits (available in the system)

openRefrigerator.title: Open the refrigerator
openRefrigerator.body: For no more than 30 seconds, otherwise warm outside air will distort the reading.

measureTemperature.title: Measure the temperature
measureTemperature.body: Place the probe between products in the middle area, NOT by the door or fan.
measureTemperature.tip: Also check the built-in thermometer if present. A difference >2°C means calling an engineer.

recordTemperature.title: Record the temperature
recordTemperature.body: Enter the reading in the field for each refrigerator. Compare with the limits:
recordTemperature.tip: Ready-to-eat food refrigerator: 0…+6°C. Perishables refrigerator: 0…+4°C. Freezer: −18…−25°C.

actImmediately.title: Act immediately if outside the limits
actImmediately.body: 1) Move contents to another refrigerator. 2) Record the corrective action. 3) Call an engineer. 4) If outside the limits for >6 hours, dispose of the food.

breakdown.label: Breakdown
breakdown.value: Refrigerator No. 2 (perishables): +12°C. Action: contents moved to R-1, engineer called (12:40), food inspected and appears normal, held pending a check. After return: <+4°C.

mistakes.openDoorMeasurement: Measuring with the door open: readings will always look “better”
mistakes.notMovingFood: Not moving food during a breakdown: the most dangerous consequence

unknownWarmDuration.trigger: Temperature >+10°C with a +4°C limit, duration unknown
unknownWarmDuration.action: DISPOSE of perishables (meat, fish, dairy and ready-to-eat food) and issue a rejection report. Do not try to salvage them: the risk of poisoning guests is very high.

freezerTooWarm.trigger: Freezer has not reached −18°C for several hours
freezerTooWarm.action: Deep-frozen storage is normally −18°C or below. At -10…-15°C for several hours, food has softened and MUST NOT be refrozen. Cook or dispose of it.

cold_equipment_control.legalRef: Customs Union Technical Regulation 021/2011, Article 17; Technical Regulation 034/2013 (meat); SanPiN 2.3/2.4.4282-26 (journal form: Appendix No. 2).

intensive_cooling.intro: The rapid cooling journal for hot dishes records a HACCP critical control point (CCP). The aim is to pass through the danger zone (+60…+10°C) in <2 hours before bacteria can multiply.
intensive_cooling.whoFills: The cook who prepared the dish. Do not delegate: the person who cooked it also cools it.
intensive_cooling.whenToFill: Whenever a hot dish needs cooling for later reheating.

prepare.chiller: Blast chiller or dedicated ice bath

recordStart.title: Record the starting temperature
recordStart.body: Immediately after cooking, before placing in the cold. It must be >65°C. A lower temperature means the dish is already unsafe.

placeInChiller.title: Use the blast chiller or ice bath
placeInChiller.body: Cut large pieces into portions no thicker than 8 cm. Put liquid dishes in shallow trays, no deeper than 5 cm. Otherwise, the centre will not cool in time.
placeInChiller.tip: Required: from +60°C to +10°C in no more than 2 hours; preferably within 90 minutes.

recordInterim.title: Record the intermediate temperature
recordInterim.body: Measure after 1 hour. If still >+30°C, speed cooling up by stirring or moving to a colder place.

recordFinal.title: Record the final temperature
recordFinal.body: After 2 hours it must be ≤+10°C. Record the reading and move the dish to a regular refrigerator for storage.

normal.label: OK
normal.value: Broth, 30 L: 75°C → 28°C (60 min) → 8°C (110 min). Within limits.

tooSlow.label: Exceeded 2 hours
tooSlow.value: Chicken in sauce: 70°C → 35°C (60 min) → 12°C (130 min). Corrective action: reheat to 75°C and serve the same day; do NOT keep until tomorrow.

mistakes.hotPotInRefrigerator: Putting a hot stockpot straight into a regular refrigerator raises its temperature and spoils all the food inside
mistakes.largeMeatPieces: Not cutting a large piece of meat: the centre stays hot
mistakes.closedLid: Putting a lid on traps steam and slows cooling

stillWarm.action: Reheat the dish to 75°C for at least 2 minutes, then repeat cooling in the blast chiller. If it happens again, DISPOSE of the dish.

intensive_cooling.legalRef: Federal Research Centre of Nutrition HACCP guidance (CCP-3 “Cooling”); Customs Union Technical Regulation 021/2011.

fryer_oil.intro: Quality control for frying oil. Overheated or old oil is carcinogenic (acrylamide and polar compounds).
fryer_oil.whoFills: The hot kitchen cook, at the start and end of the shift.
fryer_oil.whenToFill: Daily. Change oil according to schedule or earlier if results are poor.

prepare.polarTester: Polar compound tester, such as 3M strips or equivalent

inspectVisually.title: Inspect visually
inspectVisually.body: Pour a little into a clear glass. Oil should be clear and amber. Dark brown, cloudy oil with a burnt smell must be replaced.

testPolarCompounds.title: Test polar compounds
testPolarCompounds.body: Dip the strip in hot oil (170°C) for 10 seconds. Compare with the scale on the packaging. More than 25% polar compounds means immediate replacement.
testPolarCompounds.tip: Polar compounds are decomposition products. Customs Union Technical Regulation 024/2011 sets a limit of 25%.

recordResult.title: Record the result
recordResult.body: Fill “Colour”, “Smell”, “Polar compounds %” and “Last replacement date”. If changing the oil, select “Replaced today”.

normal.label: OK
normal.value: Colour: amber; smell: normal; polar compounds: 12%; replaced 5 days ago.

replacement.label: Replacement
replacement.value: Colour: dark brown; smell: burnt; polar compounds: 28%. → Drain, clean the fryer and refill with fresh oil. Recorded use: 12 L.

mistakes.toppingUp: Adding fresh oil to old oil instead of replacing it: the fresh oil deteriorates within hours
mistakes.noPolarTest: Assessing oil only by eye, without a polar compound tester
mistakes.missingReplacementDate: Not recording the replacement date makes the frequency impossible to prove
mistakes.unsafeFiltering: Filtering hot oil over an open container without protection risks burns and foreign matter contamination
mistakes.leftOnOvernight: Leaving the fryer on overnight so it heats up faster in the morning

smokingOil.action: Switch off immediately and replace the oil: its smoke point has fallen and it has decomposed. Withdraw food fried in this batch of oil from sale.

highPolarCompounds.trigger: Tester shows more than 25% polar compounds
highPolarCompounds.action: Drain the oil, remove carbon deposits from the bowl and heating elements, and add fresh oil. Record the drained volume and complete a write-off.

foamAndRancidity.trigger: Oil foams and has a sharp rancid smell
foamAndRancidity.action: Replace without delay. Check whether water or breading entered the bowl: both greatly accelerate decomposition.

fryer_oil.legalRef: Customs Union Technical Regulation 024/2011, “Safety of fats and oils”; Methodological Guidelines 2.3.2.721-98.

disinfectant_usage.intro: Track disinfectant receipts, usage and working solution concentrations. Confirm that solutions are not diluted by guesswork.
disinfectant_usage.whoFills: The senior cleaner or cleaning manager.
disinfectant_usage.whenToFill: When receiving a new batch, preparing a new working solution and recording daily use.

recordReceipt.title: Record the receipt
recordReceipt.body: Supplier, date, quantity, batch number and expiry date. Attach the certificate of conformity.

prepareSolution.title: Prepare the working solution
prepareSolution.body: Follow the packaging instructions. For example, “Profimax 2%” means 20 ml concentrate per 1 L of water. Do NOT estimate.
prepareSolution.tip: Too weak: ineffective. Too strong: residues on dishes and chemical burns.

recordUsage.title: Record usage
recordUsage.body: Record how many litres of working solution were used during the shift.

disinfectant_usage.legalRef: SanPiN 3.3686-21 and the disinfectant manufacturer’s instructions.

equipment_cleaning.intro: The equipment washing and disinfection journal. Every appliance, including mixers, slicers, mincers and ovens, must be cleaned according to schedule.
equipment_cleaning.whoFills: The cook or cleaner who used the equipment.
equipment_cleaning.whenToFill: After every shift or after handling each type of raw material; meat and fish require immediate washing.

disassemble.title: Disassemble the appliance
disassemble.body: Remove working parts according to the instructions: mincer plate and blade, slicer disc.

wash.title: Wash in hot water with detergent
wash.body: Water temperature ≥45°C; use an approved detergent. Soak for 10 minutes.

disinfect.title: Disinfect
disinfect.body: Apply disinfectant for 5–10 minutes, then rinse under running water.

dryAndAssemble.title: Dry and reassemble
dryAndAssemble.body: Air-dry or use a disposable towel. Do not wipe with a cloth, which can carry germs.

recordCleaning.title: Record in the journal
recordCleaning.body: Appliance, time, product and person who cleaned it.

sanitary_day_control.intro: Monthly sanitary day checklist. See the “Deep cleaning journal” for details.
sanitary_day_control.whoFills: The cleaning team, supervised by the manager.

completeChecklist.title: Complete the checklist
completeChecklist.body: For each item in order, record what was done, by whom and when. Sign at the bottom.

incoming_raw_materials_control.intro: The same as “Product receiving”: a combined journal.

metal_impurity.intro: A register of metal impurities in raw materials. Flour, spices and grains must pass a magnetic trap or metal detector before use.
metal_impurity.whenToFill: Whenever a bag or package of loose raw material is opened.

passThroughMagnet.title: Pass raw materials through the magnet
passThroughMagnet.body: Use a standard catering magnetic trap. An industrial metal detector is preferable if available.

recordResult.title: Record the result
recordResult.body: If nothing is found, enter “Absent”. Otherwise describe the item (shavings, paper clip or bolt), complete a report and return the goods to the supplier.

metal_impurity.legalRef: Customs Union Technical Regulation 021/2011; HACCP metal control (CCP).

traceability_test.intro: Product traceability journal. Run quarterly drills to trace a batch from supplier to the guest’s plate, so the source can be found quickly after an incident.
traceability_test.whenToFill: Quarterly, according to the audit plan.

traceBack.title: Reconstruct the chain backwards
traceBack.body: Ingredients used in the borscht → ingredient batches → suppliers → dates. This must be traceable within 30 minutes.

recordResult.title: Record the result
recordResult.body: If the chain was reconstructed, mark “Success”. Resolve any missing links.

product_writeoff.intro: A rejection report is the official product write-off document. Accounting needs it to record costs; HACCP needs it as evidence that unsafe raw materials were removed.
product_writeoff.whoFills: A commission of 3: head chef, commodity expert and manager.
product_writeoff.whenToFill: Whenever a batch or individual product unit is written off.

describeProduct.title: Describe the product and quantity
describeProduct.body: Name, batch number, production date, quantity in kg, litres or units, and value.

stateReason.title: State the reason
stateReason.body: Expiry, damaged integrity, temperature incident, sensory deviation and so on.

disposalMethod.title: Choose the disposal method
disposalMethod.body: Usually, seal in a bag labelled “Disposal” for normal waste collection. Hazardous waste, such as large quantities of spoiled meat, needs specialist disposal.

collectSignatures.title: All commission members sign
collectSignatures.body: Without all 3 signatures the report is invalid and accounting will not accept it.

product_writeoff.legalRef: Customs Union Technical Regulation 021/2011, Article 21; HACCP disposal procedures.

equipment_calibration.intro: An instrument verification schedule. Thermometers, scales and psychrometers must be verified annually by an accredited laboratory.
equipment_calibration.whenToFill: On receipt of a verification certificate; set a reminder for 30 days before expiry.

registerInstrument.title: Add the instrument to the register
registerInstrument.body: Type (thermometer, scales or hygrometer), model, serial number, verification date and next due date.

uploadCertificate.title: Upload the verification certificate
uploadCertificate.body: A PDF with the laboratory stamp, retained for the inspector.

respondToExpiry.title: Act before expiry
