alreadyDone.locked: The entry is already saved. Company rules allow only administrators to edit completed entries. Ask your manager to correct the data.
alreadyDone.editable: The entry is already saved. You can open it to edit the data. The previous values will be replaced.

confirm.title: Check the data
confirm.description: After confirmation, the entry will be added to the WeSetup journal.

pipeline.title: Step-by-step completion
pipeline.commentPlaceholder: What did you notice at this step that should be recorded?
pipeline.allDone: All steps are complete. Add a comment and select “Done”.

verify.error: Could not submit the decision. Try again.
verify.rejectedToast: Returned for correction. The employee will be notified.

help.body: 💬 WeSetup on Telegram For staff • /start — home screen • /shift — my shift · start/end in one tap • /tasks — tasks to fill in today • /my_digest — the same tasks as a chat list • /journals — SanPiN and HACCP logs • /me — my profile For managers • /today — today’s summary (X / Y logs) • /missing — incomplete items (with names) • /staff — who is on shift today • /capa — open CAPA tickets • /batches — active batches • /losses — weekly write-offs • /stats — weekly completion chart • /who_late — who has been on shift for more than 2h without log entries • /health — bot diagnostics (build sha, DB, Telegram API) • /reports — PDF and inspector ZIP Other • Any text — ask support here; replies come to this chat • /stop — unlink Telegram Support: message us at @wesetupbot — we’ll reply personally. index.metadataTitle: WeSetup features — digital HACCP and SanPiN logs
index.metadataDescription: What WeSetup does: iiko and 1C sync, log autofill, staff reminders, temperature monitoring, and role-based access.
index.title: What WeSetup does for you
index.intro: Fill in logs from your phone in minutes; some entries are completed automatically on schedule. See how it works, from accounting-system sync to reminders during a shift.
index.catalogDescription: Browse all {journalCount, plural, one {# log} other {# logs}} with examples: what to record, how often, and which requirement calls for it.

detail.trialDescription: The free plan is free forever and includes all features and integrations. No card required.

qr.title: Fill in logs with QR codes
qr.tagline: Place a sticker where readings are taken: on a refrigerator, by the changing-room thermometer, on a UV lamp, or on a fryer. Staff scan it with a phone, enter a PIN and a reading, and the entry goes straight into the SanPiN-formatted log.
qr.intro: Fill in the log beside the equipment, not from memory at the end of a shift. Scan the sticker with the phone's regular camera to open the right log page. No app installation or account sign-in is needed.
qr.stickersFridges: Refrigerators and freezers each get their own sticker. The temperature is recorded in today's column of the temperature-control log.
qr.stickersChangingRoom: In the changing room, by the thermometer: staff complete three fields in the hygiene log, and the check is also added to the health log.
qr.stickersLamps: Germicidal lamps have two buttons: “I turned it on” and “I turned it off.” Operating time and remaining lamp life are calculated automatically.
qr.stickersFryers: For fryers, the fat type, product, and quality assessment are entered as a row in the frying-oil log.
qr.stickersStorage: Warehouses and rooms: temperature and humidity.
qr.stickersGeneral: A general log QR code is available for logs not tied to equipment.
qr.record1: A staff member scans the sticker with the phone camera.
qr.record2: They select themselves from the list; the phone can remember the selection.
qr.record3: They enter their personal 4–6 digit PIN.
qr.record4: They enter the reading and tap “Save.” The server records the time.
qr.issue1: If a temperature is outside the limit, the form asks what action was taken and notifies the log owner in Telegram.
qr.issue2: If an employee does not complete the field for a temperature above 37 °C or symptoms, they are not cleared to work and the manager is notified immediately.
qr.issue3: If today's log is incomplete, the manager gets reminders at 12:00, 17:00, and 21:00.
qr.startText: Add equipment in settings, print the stickers on an A4 sheet, and put them in place. Where Wi-Fi sensors are installed, temperatures are written to the log automatically, without scanning.

sync-iiko-1c.title: Sync with iiko and 1C
sync-iiko-1c.tagline: Items, suppliers, and delivery notes flow into WeSetup automatically, so quality checks and incoming inspections need little manual entry.
sync-iiko-1c.intro: Manual copying from paper or electronic delivery notes is a major source of errors in quality-check and receiving logs. WeSetup connects directly to iiko or 1C and imports the same items, deliveries, and units of measure already in your accounting system.
sync-iiko-1c.sync1: Supplier directory, including tax IDs and contracts.
sync-iiko-1c.sync3: Receipts: each delivery note appears in incoming inspection.
sync-iiko-1c.sync4: Write-offs: quality-check results are sent automatically to the accounting system.
sync-iiko-1c.sync5: Warehouse stock, linked to storage-temperature monitoring.
sync-iiko-1c.humanText: Actual measurements: product temperature on receipt, sensory assessment, and the responsible employee's signature. These must not be filled in automatically; the point of the log is for a person to take the measurement.
sync-iiko-1c.connectText: In iiko, connect with a token from your account; in 1C, use the standard data-exchange module. The initial 30-day import usually takes 10–15 minutes.

autofill.title: Automatic log filling
autofill.tagline: Routine values are filled in automatically, so staff confirm what happened instead of copying the same figures shift after shift.
autofill.intro: Autofill is a configurable tool. WeSetup can fill in predictable values that do not depend on the exact moment, such as a shift, days-off schedule, or job title. It deliberately does not fill in readings that must be measured or observed.
autofill.automatic1: Days off, vacation, and sick-leave marks in the hygiene log.
autofill.automatic2: An employee's job title when they are added to a shift.
autofill.automatic3: Reference fields in a log header: date, shift number, and responsible person.
autofill.automatic4: A “normal conditions” mark for temperature readings within the permitted range.
autofill.forbidden3: Sensory assessment of incoming raw materials.
autofill.forbidden4: Whether an employee is cleared to work according to the health log.
autofill.cautionText: WeSetup has no “close the shift with zeros” mode. An incomplete log stays open and appears in the manager's morning report. That is safer than falsifying records.

cloud.title: Everything in the cloud
cloud.tagline: Access logs from a computer, tablet, or phone. History stays available for as long as the law requires.
cloud.intro: WeSetup runs in the cloud: no local servers or backup setup, and no need to decide where to keep last year's records. Backups run automatically, and history remains available when you replace a computer or move your business.
cloud.device1: Manager's computer: full reports, analytics, and settings.
cloud.device2: Kitchen tablet: large buttons and convenient entry, even with gloves.
cloud.device3: Employee phone: quick hygiene and temperature checks.
cloud.device4: Telegram bot: reminders and notifications without signing in to the system.
cloud.securityText: HTTPS, individual logins, an activity log for each user, and storage under Russian jurisdiction. Even an owner cannot delete an entry retroactively; they can only mark it corrected and provide a reason.
cloud.retentionText: SanPiN logs: 12 months; HACCP logs and audits: 3 years. WeSetup keeps history for the subscription period and 60 days afterward.

role-access.title: Role-based access
role-access.tagline: Employees see only their assigned logs. Managers see everyone's. Owners can close a period and export a PDF with one click.
role-access.intro: Different people in the kitchen and dining room have different responsibilities. WeSetup provides three access levels so employees see what they need while managers keep full oversight.
role-access.level1: Owner / Manager: sees all logs, locations, and dates; closes periods and edits templates.
role-access.level2: Head chef / Technologist: sees their department, manages quality checks, and assigns responsible staff.
role-access.level3: Cook / Waiter: sees only assigned logs and cannot change another person's entries.
role-access.aclText: With ACL, a manager can grant an employee access to a log outside their role. For example, a night-shift cook can access the UV-lamp log while other employees cannot.
role-access.auditText: Every ACL change appears in the activity log, showing who granted or removed a person's access and when.

reminders.title: Shift reminders
reminders.tagline: Telegram and email remind staff when a log is still incomplete near the end of a shift. In the morning, the logs are closed and the manager can rest easy.
reminders.intro: Missed entries are often caused by interruptions, not forgetfulness. When it is time to record a temperature, the next task may already be underway. WeSetup sends a reminder when a log is not complete, to the responsible employee and a copy to the manager.
reminders.channel1: Telegram bot: an instant message to the employee.
reminders.channel2: Email: a copy to the manager if the employee does not respond.
reminders.channel3: Web push: a banner in the manager's browser.
reminders.channel4: Daily summary: delivered to the manager's inbox in the morning.
reminders.scheduleText: Reminders follow the shift schedule and its end time. The first arrives 30 minutes before closing, the second 5 minutes before. After closing, the manager receives a report of incomplete logs.
reminders.smsText: SMS is expensive in Russia and can be delayed. Telegram and email arrive quickly and at no extra charge, and food-service employees usually already have Telegram installed.

alerts.title: Alerts for deviations
alerts.tagline: An out-of-range temperature, an overdue item, or a failed quality check triggers a notification right away, not at the end of the shift.
alerts.intro: A reminder and an alert describe different events. A reminder says, “Don't forget to fill this in.” An alert says, “A deviation occurred; action is needed.” WeSetup keeps these streams separate so important events are not lost among routine notifications.
alerts.trigger1: A refrigerator temperature stays outside its limit for at least 30 minutes.
alerts.trigger2: An employee with acute respiratory symptoms is marked as not cleared for the shift.
alerts.trigger3: A raw-material batch fails incoming inspection.
alerts.trigger4: A dish fails its quality check.
alerts.recipientsText: Alerts can be routed by role and location. Temperature alerts go to the head chef and manager; an employee suspension goes to HR and the director; financially significant write-offs go to the owner. Each event type can have its own route.
alerts.capaText: Each alert creates a CAPA record with an owner and due date. It stays on the open list until the CAPA is closed; it cannot simply disappear as “handled.”

paperless.title: No more paper
paperless.tagline: No need to buy standard logs, print forms, or store boxes. Entries are electronic from the moment they are recorded.
paperless.intro: Paper logs are an annual expense and a steady source of problems: they get lost or damaged, or arrive late from a supplier. During an inspection, staff have to pull them out of boxes, and some may be missing. An electronic log solves these problems at once.
paperless.stop1: Standard SanPiN and HACCP logs to purchase.
paperless.stop2: Archive shelves and boxes of binders.
paperless.stop3: Scanning logs and sending them to an auditor.
paperless.stop4: One-off printouts “for an inspection”; a PDF is generated in seconds.
paperless.signatureText: If an inspector asks for a signed original, print the PDF, sign it in blue ink, and keep it until the inspection is over. After that, you can go back to paperless work.
paperless.savingsText: An average food-service location spends 8,000–12,000 rubles a year on paper logs and printing—about two months of a WeSetup subscription.

time-saving.title: Save time
time-saving.tagline: Five to ten minutes at the end of a shift instead of an hour of paperwork. Cooks get home on time, and the head chef has no pile of forms to reconcile.
time-saving.intro: One of the most overlooked benefits of an electronic log is the time it saves in the kitchen. This is based on measurements we take during each rollout: an hour of routine work falls to 5–10 minutes because duplicate entry and copying disappear.
time-saving.source1: No duplicate entry: receipts flow into quality checks and stock automatically.
time-saving.source2: Headers fill automatically: no need to enter the date, shift, and responsible person every time.
time-saving.source3: Group write-off: one check mark for five items creates one entry instead of five.
time-saving.source4: Generate an auditor's PDF in seconds instead of photographing paper forms.
time-saving.networksText: One manager can oversee five locations instead of five head chefs each spending an hour reconciling records. The savings show up in payroll, not just hours.
time-saving.closing: Our internal measurements show that after the first two weeks, employees stop treating log entry as “separate work.” It becomes part of the shift, like closing the register.

descriptions.hygiene: Keeps people with symptoms of acute respiratory viral infections, gastrointestinal infections or pustular skin lesions away from food handling. Completed for each employee on every shift.
descriptions.health_check: An expanded hygiene log that records each symptom as well as the admission decision, useful when investigating food poisoning.
descriptions.climate_control: Food cannot be kept safe in a storeroom at 30 °C and 85% humidity. The log records whether the indoor conditions meet storage requirements.
descriptions.cold_equipment_control: Refrigerators are a HACCP critical control point. At least once per shift, readings are checked against an external thermometer and the standard for the specific product.
descriptions.cleaning_ventilation_checklist: Fresh air and clean surfaces are basic sanitation. The log confirms that the procedures were carried out and signed off by a named person.
descriptions.cleaning: Daily routine cleaning: which rooms were cleaned, which detergents and disinfectants were used, who carried out the work and who checked it.
descriptions.general_cleaning: A full deep clean once per period (week / month), including removing protective grilles, washing walls and cleaning equipment. The inspector checks both the plan and the completed work.
descriptions.uv_lamp_runtime: The lamp has a limited service life (8000 hours for most models). The log tracks operating hours and replacements; otherwise UV treatment becomes ineffective after the lamp reaches the end of its life.
descriptions.finished_product: A key HACCP and SanPiN checkpoint: before a dish is served in the dining room, it must pass an organoleptic check. The log records the commission’s assessment.
descriptions.perishable_rejection: Incoming checks for dairy, meat and fish products: safety documents, organoleptic assessment, storage conditions and the final sale date of each batch.
descriptions.incoming_control: Comprehensive incoming checks cover supplier documentation, labeling and conformity with the delivery note. This protects against deliveries without a certificate.
descriptions.fryer_oil: Overheated oil produces carcinogens. The log records temperature, acid value and oil changes to keep spent oil out of dishes.
descriptions.med_books: Every employee at a food business must have a valid personal medical record book. The log shows whose records are nearing expiry.
descriptions.training_plan: HACCP requires regular refresher briefings, not just a one-off introduction. The plan schedules who covers which topic and when.
descriptions.staff_training: Records training completed according to the plan: who attended, when, the topic and the signature. This is the first thing requested during an incident investigation.
descriptions.disinfectant_usage: Each product must have a sanitary and epidemiological certificate, be stored separately and used according to its instructions. The log confirms purchases and consumption.
descriptions.sanitary_day_control: A sanitation day is held once a month: a deep clean while the establishment is closed. The checklist records completion of each item.
descriptions.equipment_maintenance: HACCP requires evidence that equipment is in working order. A schedule paired with a record of completed work is the standard approach.
descriptions.breakdown_history: For audits: how often the refrigerator broke down, when repairs were made and what was repaired. Helps you decide on replacement in time.
descriptions.equipment_calibration: Thermometers and scales must have a valid verification certificate. Without it, their readings are not legally valid.
descriptions.incoming_raw_materials_control: The HACCP version of goods acceptance checks not only the delivery note but also the packaging, labeling and documents for every batch.
descriptions.ppe_issuance: Each employee is entitled to personal protective equipment: gloves, coats, aprons and masks. The log confirms issuance and service life.
descriptions.accident_journal: A refrigerator breakdown at night, a power outage or a leak: every incident is recorded with the measures taken and the impact on products.
descriptions.complaint_register: Complaints are an input signal for HACCP. Each one is recorded, investigated and closed with a corrective action.
descriptions.daily_samples: If someone becomes ill after lunch, the daily food sample is the only way to check exactly what was eaten. The log shows that a sample was taken from every dish, refrigerated for the required time and only then disposed of.
descriptions.vitaminization: The vitamin is added to the finished dish immediately before serving. The inspector checks that this is done daily and at the correct dose per portion.
descriptions.ration_control: Every 10 days or monthly, the record shows whether children and patients receive the required amounts of milk, meat, vegetables and other food groups, and where the diet differs from the standard.
descriptions.transport_temperature: Delivery is a separate critical point: a product may leave cold and arrive warm. Two measurements on every trip show that the cold or hot chain was not broken.
descriptions.tableware_breakage: A fragment in a dish is a physical hazard to the guest. Recording every breakage confirms that fragments were collected and disposed of, and makes recurring causes immediately visible.
descriptions.pool_water_control: Pool water must be safe for every visitor. Measurements before opening and throughout the day show that disinfection is working and that the pool was closed promptly if readings went outside the limits.
descriptions.inventory_condition: A chipped piece of plastic or metal shavings in a dish are a physical hazard. Regular inspection of knives, boards, spatulas and containers shows that damaged utensils were removed from use in time.
descriptions.instrument_sterilization: An instrument that touches a client’s skin and nails can transmit infection. Recording each sterilizer load and its indicator result confirms that the instruments actually completed the cycle rather than simply sitting in a cabinet.
descriptions.medical_waste_b: Used needles, blood-stained cotton pads and disposable materials from procedures must not go in household rubbish. The log traces the waste: how much was collected, how it was decontaminated, how it was packaged and who removed it.
descriptions.batch_release: A batch is sent to the customer only after checking taste, smell, appearance, labeling and packaging. The release record shows who approved the batch and on what basis, providing the foundation for traceability and complaint investigation.
descriptions.product_writeoff: Expired, defective or spoiled products are documented in a write-off report with the reason. This supports loss analysis and claims against suppliers.
descriptions.audit_plan: HACCP requires regular internal inspections: an auditor visits production areas with a checklist and records compliance with procedures.
descriptions.audit_protocol: The results of the scheduled audit: what complies and what was identified as a nonconformity.
descriptions.audit_report: A final report for management with consolidated findings, statistics and recommendations. Presented to an inspector on request.
descriptions.traceability_test: A test from delivery note to dish and back: if a guest becomes ill from food, how quickly can the full supply chain of a specific batch be traced?
descriptions.metal_impurity: Checks using a metal detector or magnetic separator on the production line protect against packaging fragments, bolts and metal shavings.
descriptions.equipment_cleaning: A separate procedure for production equipment such as mixers, water boilers and cookers. It differs from room cleaning: different products are used and the procedure is stricter.
descriptions.intensive_cooling: The range between 60 °C and 10 °C is a bacterial danger zone. HACCP requires passing through it in less than 2 hours and recording this.
descriptions.glass_items_list: An inventory of all fragile items in the production area. If something breaks, the list is checked to confirm that all fragments have been found.
descriptions.glass_control: Records glass breakage, the search for fragments and the decision on what to do with the products.
descriptions.pest_control: Scheduled treatments by a contractor or in-house staff: completion, product used and purpose. No serious audit is complete without this log.

hygiene.title: Hygiene log — a sample for food service
hygiene.description: Hygiene log under SanPiN 2.3/2.4.4282-26: automatic filling, work clearance, temperature checks and PDF for Rospotrebnadzor. Free forever.
hygiene.seoIntro: The electronic food service hygiene log complies with SanPiN 2.3/2.4.4282-26 and the Rospotrebnadzor order. Employee work clearance, symptoms and temperature, and the responsible person's signature are all on one screen, without paper or manual comparison with the timesheet.

health_check.title: Health log (ЗОЖ): conducting pre-shift checks
health_check.description: How to conduct daily pre-shift checks: who examines staff, which signs to record, when to remove someone from work and how to document refused clearance.
health_check.seoIntro: The health log is a detailed examination form. It records every symptom, not just work clearance, which is useful when investigating food poisoning. The electronic version records the examination time, removal from work and corrective actions.

climate_control.title: Premises temperature and humidity log
climate_control.description: Premises temperature and humidity log: sensors, automatic readings and ventilation schedules. Limits are set for each room; deviations go straight to the responsible person.
climate_control.seoIntro: A warehouse temperature and humidity log is a mandatory SanPiN item for rooms where food is stored: it confirms microclimate monitoring. In WeSetup, sensors take readings every 5–10 minutes, and deviations automatically go to CAPA.

cold_equipment_control.title: Refrigerator temperature log: limits and recordkeeping
cold_equipment_control.description: Temperature limits for refrigerators and freezers, how often to measure during a shift, who is responsible and what to do when readings leave the allowed range.
cold_equipment_control.seoIntro: The temperature log for refrigerators and freezers follows the form in Appendix No. 2 to SanPiN 2.3/2.4.4282-26. Checking refrigerator temperatures is the daily minimum. WeSetup warns when the temperature leaves the allowed range and automatically creates a CAPA with the cause, responsible person and correction deadline.

cleaning_ventilation_checklist.title: Room airing checklist
cleaning_ventilation_checklist.description: Airing and ventilation checks in the kitchen and dining area: schedules, completion marks and supply/extract system maintenance. Missed intervals are immediately visible.
cleaning_ventilation_checklist.seoIntro: The airing checklist is a simple but often forgotten SanPiN item: kitchen air changes faster than dining-area air, so the schedules differ. The electronic template inserts standard values, reminds staff about frequency and stores results alongside the ventilation maintenance schedule.

cleaning.title: Cleaning log: how to keep it and who fills it in
cleaning.description: Who fills in the cleaning log, how often and what to record: room, product, concentration, contact time and supervisor. SanPiN 2.3/2.4.4282-26 requirements.
cleaning.seoIntro: The cleaning log records every washing cycle for areas and utensils, including the cleaning product and concentration. The electronic form prevents a record from being closed with a required field missing, so the inspector always sees the complete picture.

general_cleaning.title: Deep cleaning schedule — an electronic log
general_cleaning.description: Plan and record deep cleaning: areas, products, responsible person and a signed report. Schedules cover the coming month; the system reminds you when work is due.
general_cleaning.seoIntro: Deep cleaning is a plan with dates and areas, not something left until there is time: kitchens, storage areas, dining areas and toilets are cleaned at different frequencies. WeSetup creates a monthly schedule, sends automatic reminders and generates a separate completion report for each area.

uv_lamp_runtime.title: UV lamp log — operation and operating hours
uv_lamp_runtime.description: Germicidal UV lamp log: operating hours, replacement date and safety. The 8000-9000 hour service life is counted automatically, with a reminder when it runs out.

keywords.item3: UV lamp service life in food service

uv_lamp_runtime.seoIntro: Recording germicidal UV lamp operation matters because a lamp can keep visibly glowing long after its service life ends, while its germicidal effect is already gone. WeSetup counts the hours automatically and warns about scheduled replacement; a sample completed log is available to download.

finished_product.title: Finished product quality checks: keeping the log
finished_product.description: Who sits on the food quality assessment panel, which sensory qualities to assess and which serving temperature to record. Recordkeeping under SanPiN 2.3/2.4.4282-26.
finished_product.seoIntro: The finished product quality assessment log is a key food service log; it previously followed SanPiN 2.3.2.1324-03 and now follows 2.3/2.4.4282-26. WeSetup stores assessments separately for each batch, preventing morning and lunchtime baking from being combined into one record, as required for investigating a complaint.

perishable_rejection.title: Perishable product rejection log
perishable_rejection.description: Record rejected perishable products: sensory assessment, defects, reasons and actions taken. Every rejected batch is linked to a write-off.
perishable_rejection.seoIntro: Perishable products must be checked for rejection at goods acceptance and during the shift. The electronic log links the batch to its delivery note and subsequent records, allowing its path from supplier to table to be traced in 2–4 hours.

incoming_control.title: Raw material acceptance and incoming inspection log
incoming_control.description: Incoming raw material checks: temperature on receipt, packaging, expiry dates and supplier details. Integration with iiko and 1С loads the item list automatically.
incoming_control.seoIntro: Incoming inspection of raw materials and food is the first critical point in the HACCP system. WeSetup automatically loads delivery notes from iiko and 1С; the cook records the temperature on receipt and sensory assessment without copying supplier details by hand. A sample completed log can be downloaded and printed.

fryer_oil.title: Frying oil usage log
fryer_oil.description: Frying oil records: polar compound measurements, replacement schedule, disposal and collection report. At the 24% limit, the log reminds you to change the oil.
fryer_oil.seoIntro: Frying oil records are a simple but mandatory item. The 24% polar compound limit is checked with a handheld analyzer; WeSetup saves the reading, reminds you to change the oil and stores the contractor's disposal report.

med_books.title: Employee medical record book log — electronic records
med_books.description: Employee medical record books: renewals, chest X-rays and examinations. A reminder arrives 30 days before expiry, and expired work clearance is blocked.
med_books.seoIntro: The electronic medical record book log automatically reminds you a month before a chest X-ray or scheduled examination expires. This removes the risk of an inspector finding an expired document for an employee who is working.

training_plan.title: Staff training plan
training_plan.description: Annual food service staff training plan: topics, dates, responsible person and links to the briefing log. Completed training is marked with one click.
training_plan.seoIntro: The staff training plan links topics and dates to the briefing log. WeSetup automatically creates notifications about missing items when a new employee starts a shift.

staff_training.title: Staff briefing register
staff_training.description: Record completed briefings: topic, date and signatures of the instructor and employee. Kept for three years and exported for any inspection period.
staff_training.seoIntro: Keeping a briefing register is daily practice under the training requirements for staff involved in food production and circulation. The electronic signature saves the person's full name and timestamp automatically, and a sample completed form is available to download.

disinfectant_usage.title: Disinfectant usage log
disinfectant_usage.description: Disinfectant records: consumption, concentration, application area and contact time. DDD contractor reports sit alongside the records, so nothing has to be found for an inspection.
disinfectant_usage.seoIntro: The disinfection log, also known as disinfectant records, concerns consumption and concentration rather than floor washing. WeSetup records the product, volume, application area and waiting period before production resumes. DDD contractor reports for disinfection, insect control and rodent control are also stored here; a sample completed form can be downloaded and printed.

sanitary_day_control.title: Sanitation day checklist
sanitary_day_control.description: Sanitation day guidance and checklist: areas, products, completion report and management checks. Monthly reminders arrive automatically, and unfinished work appears in a list.
sanitary_day_control.seoIntro: A sanitation day is a scheduled production shutdown for deep cleaning. The WeSetup checklist includes all required areas and becomes a completed report for inspection.

equipment_maintenance.title: Equipment maintenance log
equipment_maintenance.description: Scheduled and unscheduled food service equipment maintenance: service visits, reports, frequency and links to equipment records. The next maintenance date is calculated automatically.
equipment_maintenance.seoIntro: The equipment maintenance log is linked to the equipment record, showing the last service date, interval and next scheduled date. Emergency repairs go into the breakdown log linked to CAPA.

breakdown_history.title: Equipment breakdown history log
breakdown_history.description: Equipment breakdown history: cause, repair, write-off and contractor report. Recurring failures are immediately visible, supporting replacement instead of another repair.
breakdown_history.seoIntro: The breakdown and fault history log helps identify patterns: which equipment fails most often, what downtime costs and whether replacement pays off. WeSetup stores contractor reports and defect photos directly in the record.

equipment_calibration.title: Equipment and thermometer verification log
equipment_calibration.description: Verification of thermometers, scales and measuring instruments: frequency, certificates and links to the metrology service. The system reminds you when verification is due.
equipment_calibration.seoIntro: Thermometer and scale verification is mandatory for production facilities supplying retail chains. Calibration and verification are different procedures: the former adjusts the instrument, while the latter confirms its accuracy with a document. WeSetup automatically calculates the next verification date and attaches a scanned certificate.

incoming_raw_materials_control.title: Raw material and semi-finished goods inspection log
incoming_raw_materials_control.description: Detailed incoming inspection: certificates, laboratory reports, temperature and labeling checks. Supplier documents are stored with the goods acceptance record.
incoming_raw_materials_control.seoIntro: Incoming inspection of raw materials and semi-finished products is a mandatory HACCP requirement. WeSetup stores the test report and certificate with the record, avoiding the common mistake of keeping the papers with the accountant and the record in the cook's folder.

ppe_issuance.title: Personal protective equipment issue log
ppe_issuance.description: Record personal protective equipment issued: gloves, coats, head coverings, workwear and employee signatures. Stock levels and issue frequency are calculated automatically.
ppe_issuance.seoIntro: The PPE issue log is required by both SanPiN and the labor inspectorate. The electronic form prevents signatures from being lost: the employee signs in the Telegram bot, and the entry reaches the log in seconds.

accident_journal.title: Accident and emergency log
accident_journal.description: Record accidents, incidents and corrective measures: circumstances, people affected and action taken. Every record links to a CAPA and an investigation report.
accident_journal.seoIntro: The accident log records all unplanned events, from power outages to cleaning product spills. A record cannot be closed without a corrective action.

complaint_register.title: Complaints and claims register
complaint_register.description: Record guest complaints: contact channel, issue, responsible person, response deadline and compensation. Overdue complaints are highlighted and causes collected in a report.
complaint_register.seoIntro: The complaints log is a simple way to avoid losing guest feedback. WeSetup routes the complaint to a manager; if it recurs, it automatically opens a CAPA with a responsible person and deadline.

daily_samples.title: Daily food sample log — electronic records
daily_samples.description: Daily food sample collection and storage log for schools, kindergartens and hospitals: dish, weight, sampling time, storage temperature and disposal. Print the log with one click.
daily_samples.seoIntro: The electronic daily food sample log lets the cook select the meal and dish; the sampling date and time are filled in automatically. The inspector sees that samples were taken from every dish and stored for the required period.

vitaminization.title: Vitamin fortification log for third-course dishes
vitaminization.description: Vitamin fortification of third-course and sweet dishes: preparation, portion count, vitamin added, addition and serving times. For children's and therapeutic meals.
vitaminization.seoIntro: The electronic vitamin fortification log takes a minute to fill in, and the time the vitamin was added and the dish served are always visible side by side, exactly what the inspector checks.

ration_control.title: Dietary intake control sheet
ration_control.description: Diet control sheet: required and actual food quantities per person over 10 days or a month, with percentage deviations. For children's and medical institutions.
ration_control.seoIntro: The diet control sheet shows where actual meals differ from the standard by food group and helps adjust the next period's menu.

transport_temperature.title: Transport temperature log
transport_temperature.description: Product temperature control during transport: vehicle, route, loading and unloading temperatures. For catering, delivery and food production facilities.
transport_temperature.seoIntro: The transport temperature log covers the critical delivery point: two readings on each trip confirm that the cold or hot chain was not broken.

tableware_breakage.title: Tableware breakage log
tableware_breakage.description: Record tableware breakage in restaurants, cafés and canteens: what broke, where, why and whether fragments were collected. Physical hazard protection and clear loss statistics.
tableware_breakage.seoIntro: The tableware breakage log records every incident immediately, with the cause and confirmation that fragments were collected. It shows both the risk to guests and where breakages occur most often.

pool_water_control.title: Swimming pool water monitoring log
pool_water_control.description: Pool water quality log: temperature, free and combined chlorine, pH, clarity and visitor count. For fitness centers, sports clubs and hotels.
pool_water_control.seoIntro: The electronic pool water log lets the technician enter readings on a phone at the poolside. Deviations are immediately visible, and the inspection log prints with one click.

inventory_condition.title: Utensil condition assessment log
inventory_condition.description: Metal and plastic utensil condition log: inspection of knives, boards and containers, damage and removal from use. For kitchens and food production facilities.
inventory_condition.seoIntro: The electronic utensil condition log makes inspecting each board and spatula a matter of seconds, while damaged utensils are immediately visible and do not remain in the production area.

instrument_sterilization.title: Instrument sterilization monitoring log
instrument_sterilization.description: Instrument sterilization log for beauty salons and nail studios: method, cycle settings, indicator and sterilizer. Electronic records with printing for inspections.

keywords.item2: nail studio dry heat sterilizer log

instrument_sterilization.seoIntro: The electronic sterilization log lets the practitioner record a dry heat sterilizer or autoclave load from a phone, while the administrator sees that every cycle was completed with an indicator.

medical_waste_b.title: Class Б waste log
medical_waste_b.description: Class Б waste log: waste type and quantity, decontamination, packaging and handover to the collection organization. For salons offering cosmetology and medical practices.

keywords.item1: class Б waste in beauty salons

medical_waste_b.seoIntro: The class Б waste log traces every package from the treatment room to handover to the collection organization, without paper notebooks.

batch_release.title: Product batch release for shipment log
batch_release.description: Release finished product batches for shipment: batch number, quantity, sensory, labeling and packaging checks, and the responsible person's decision. For production and bakeries.
batch_release.seoIntro: The batch release log records who released the products and which checks preceded release. The batch number makes the record easy to find if a customer makes a claim.

product_writeoff.title: Product write-off log
product_writeoff.description: Write off expired, rejected or returned products: reason, weight and responsible person. Links to iiko and 1С inventory remove written-off items without duplicate entry.
product_writeoff.seoIntro: The product write-off log closes the gap between the warehouse and kitchen. Expiry write-offs reach iiko and 1С in real time, so the inspector sees the same stock on the shelf and in the record.

audit_plan.title: Internal audit plan and program
audit_plan.description: Annual HACCP internal audit plan: topics, frequency, auditors and links to audit records and reports. Missed audits are visible before an inspector asks about them.
audit_plan.seoIntro: The internal audit plan and program is the first document an auditor starts with. WeSetup creates the annual plan, assigns auditors and links every inspection to its audit record and report.

audit_protocol.title: Internal audit record
audit_protocol.description: Record the audit process: date, area, auditor, factual observations, nonconformities and evidence. The report and corrective actions are assembled from the record automatically.
audit_protocol.seoIntro: The internal audit record is the audit team's working document. WeSetup allows photographic evidence of nonconformities to be attached directly to the relevant record item.

audit_report.title: Internal audit report
audit_report.description: Final internal audit report: nonconformities with severity levels, CAPA, correction deadlines and the manager's signature. Overdue actions are highlighted.
audit_report.seoIntro: The internal audit report is a management document. The manager reads it and uses it to decide on CAPA and investments. WeSetup generates the report automatically from audit records and classifies nonconformities by severity.

traceability_test.title: Traceability test log
traceability_test.description: Periodic traceability test: a random batch, reconstructing its path from supplier to table and checking response time. The required window is two to four hours.
traceability_test.seoIntro: The traceability test is a quarterly exercise: for a randomly selected batch, the team must reconstruct the chain within 2–4 hours. WeSetup splits the chain into stages and automatically times each step.

metal_impurity.title: Metal contamination control log
metal_impurity.description: Metal contamination control log: metal detector checks, frequency, calibration and detection reports. Every detection is linked to the batch's disposition.
metal_impurity.seoIntro: Metal contamination control is required in food production. WeSetup records metal detector activations and periodic calibration, linking them to the instrument's maintenance reports.

equipment_cleaning.title: Equipment washing and disinfection log
equipment_cleaning.description: Washing and disinfection of slicers, mixers, ovens and ice makers: products, concentrations, contact time and swab tests. Equipment is the number one cross-contamination source.
equipment_cleaning.seoIntro: Equipment washing and disinfection has its own log because equipment is the number one source of cross-contamination. WeSetup inserts the selected product and counts the contact time automatically, preventing the disinfectant from being rinsed off too soon.

intensive_cooling.title: Rapid cooling log
intensive_cooling.description: Rapid cooling control for finished products: from +65 to +10 °C in two hours. Blast chiller, sensor and automatic report; excess time is recorded and sent to CAPA.
intensive_cooling.seoIntro: Rapid cooling of finished products is a HACCP critical point. Limit: +65 → +10 °C in 2 hours. WeSetup collects sensor readings in the blast freezer and generates a completed report.

glass_items_list.title: Glassware inventory log
glass_items_list.description: Kitchen glass item inventory: availability, quantities and regular integrity checks. Breakage or missing items are immediately linked to the glass control log.
glass_items_list.seoIntro: The glassware inventory log helps prevent fragments from entering a dish. WeSetup stores the list, and each inventory check shows that everything is in place.

glass_control.title: Glass control log
glass_control.description: Check glass and mirror integrity in production areas: record breakage, investigate and withdraw products. Every incident automatically creates a CAPA ticket.
glass_control.seoIntro: Glass control is a HACCP point in major production facilities. Every breakage incident opens a CAPA and links to the glass item inventory, so the inspector sees the complete control cycle.

pest_control.title: Disinfection, insect and rodent control log
pest_control.description: Scheduled DDD treatment records: contractor, product, site, waiting period and reports. The contract and reports sit beside the schedule, the first things an inspector requests.
pest_control.seoIntro: The disinfection, insect and rodent control log is mandatory for any thorough inspection. WeSetup attaches the contractor's report directly to the record and automatically blocks production during the waiting period after treatment.

publicJournalDetailFaq.fieldsAnswer: Required fields: {fields}. An empty field is equivalent to an incomplete log for an inspector, so use a dash deliberately and include an explanation.

cadence.sanpin_daily: Every shift: make the entry on the day of the event. Do not backdate entries: uniform dates and identical values are precisely how inspectors identify record keeping done only as a formality.
cadence.sanpin_periodic: According to the schedule, rather than daily: the frequency is set in the production control programme and must match the actual records.
cadence.haccp: According to the HACCP plan: the frequency is set when describing the control point and justified in the plan itself.

publicJournalDetailFaq.normativeAnswer: {norms}. Include the regulatory reference on the title page so the inspector can immediately see why the log is kept.
publicJournalDetailFaq.electronicAnswer: Yes. SanPiN 2.3/2.4.4282-26 does not require paper: the important points are being able to see who made an entry and when, and preventing unnoticed retrospective changes. For an inspection, print the electronic log for the required period.
publicJournalDetailFaq.retentionAnswer: Inspectors usually request records for the last 12 months, so one year is a practical minimum. Keep logs connected with a food poisoning investigation or a complaint until the proceedings are closed.
